title: Agent docs ship an API reference and a compact feature index
detail: `packages/framework/agents/` now contains `api.md` with one file per app-facing entry point (engine, errors, ui-types, db, event-store, seeding, renderer/web, testing/stack, testing/helpers, dev-server/testing) plus `api/types.md` for the types they reference. Signatures are one line each, option types are property lists with the first doc sentence, and `@internal` declarations are left out. `features-index.md` lists every bundled feature with one sentence, the import of its factory, its required features, config keys without a default and secrets. `AGENTS.md` points agents at the index first and at `api.md` instead of `dist/*.d.ts`. Both files are generated by `bun run gen:agent-docs` and checked by the agent-docs-drift guard.

title: Opt-in anonymous uploads per file field
detail: Since the upload route rejects anonymous callers, `POST /api/files` answered 401 for every anonymous visitor. A file, image, files or images field with `anonymousUpload: true` now accepts a pending upload from an anonymous visitor (entityType and fieldName, no entityId, no actionForm); the app binds the file itself. Everything else stays 401 for anonymous callers.

title: jose updated to 6.2.13
detail: Dependency bump of jose in framework and bundled-features. No API change for consumers.

title: Scrub primitive for event payload fields
detail: Plaintext written before a field was declared personal without a subject to erase, or a ciphertext that no longer decrypts, stayed in `kumiko_events`, and the only way out was a raw `UPDATE` on the event store, which the event-store-writes guard rejects. The scrub walks the events of one type in batches, reaches the `changes` and `previous` sections of entity lifecycle events, lets `shouldScrub(value, candidate)` narrow the values (for example to those that throw `PiiCiphertextCorruptError`), drops the snapshots of touched streams and queues the affected projection and multi-stream projection tables in `kumiko_pending_rebuilds` in the same transaction, then rebuilds them; a failed rebuild stays queued. `reason` is required and placeholders are refused; `dryRun` only counts.

title: jsonb fields can default to an empty array
detail: A jsonb field that stores a list had the fixed column default `{}`, so a row that never wrote it read an object while every other row read an array, and the generated write schema only accepted plain objects. `emptyValue: "array"` switches the column default to `[]` and the write schema to an array; the default stays `"object"`. The schema migration renders `ALTER COLUMN ... SET DEFAULT '[]'::jsonb`; existing rows that never wrote the field get `[]` with the next rebuild of the projection.

title: Abandoned form uploads can expire
detail: An upload sent with entityType and fieldName but without a record stays pending until a save binds it. When the form was abandoned, the fileRef row and its bytes stayed forever without an owner that deletes them. With `pendingUploadGraceHours` the `files:job:sweep-orphaned-uploads` job soft-deletes such rows through the fileRef executor once they are older than the grace period. Uploads without a target field (inbox, dropzone) and files the system user created are kept. It is opt-in because an app that stores fileRef ids without binding them would lose those files.

title: Corrupt PII ciphertext has its own error type
detail: `decryptPiiFieldValues`, `decryptPiiValueForSubject` and every read path built on them threw Node's generic "unable to authenticate data" error for a failed GCM auth tag, the same shape as any other failure. Now a failed auth tag, an AAD mismatch (value copied into another field or subject), a malformed ciphertext and an undecodable jsonb plaintext throw `PiiCiphertextCorruptError` with the field name; it is a KumikoError, so it keeps its code through the dispatcher. An export can blank one such row and still fail loud on an outage, which keeps its own `EncryptionUnavailableError`.

title: sortNulls places rows without a value in list sorting
detail: Without the option the list keeps Postgres' order (nulls last ascending, first descending), which a plain index serves. With `sortNulls` the list query adds `NULLS FIRST` or `NULLS LAST` to the order and the keyset cursor follows it, so paging across the rows without a value stays complete. A sort that must stay on an index needs an index with the same NULLS order.

title: Transition guard ignores an unchanged state value
detail: An update whose `changes` carry the state field with the value the row already has is no transition, so the guard skips it instead of rejecting it as a self-transition that the map does not list. Before, a rename on a `sold` or `finished` row failed as soon as the client sent the current status along.

title: Entity writes on a row the caller cannot read fail with not_found
detail: update, delete, restore and forget only checked access.write, so on an entity with an owner access.read rule and no access.write any tenant member with handler access could change or delete another member's row, and delete returned the decrypted row. They now apply the same access.read rule and parentRef host-visibility gate as detail and answer not_found, so the row's existence stays hidden. Framework system writes are exempt. A write the caller could not read but that failed the write rule before now reports not_found instead of ownership_denied.
migration: Writes on rows the caller cannot read now fail with not_found; give such writers read access or run them as system. Custom handlers that call the executor directly get the parentRef gate by passing parentVisibility: { entities: ctx.registry.getAllEntities() }, as the generated handlers do.

title: A file upload with an ended session ends up at the login
detail: POST /files answered an anonymous caller (revoked or expired session) with 403 forbidden or a validation error, so the browser showed an upload error instead of the login. Anonymous callers can never use an upload (they cannot bind pending files), so every upload without a session now answers 401 with code unauthenticated before the body is read, and the file upload fields signal the ended session like any other request. Signed-in callers without permission still get 403.

title: AGENTS.md points app tests at kumiko-dev-server/testing
detail: The Tests section told agents to import setupAppTestStack and seedTenant from @cosmicdrift/kumiko-testing, which does not export them; an agent that followed it got a missing-export error and had to copy the import from the scaffolded test. The section now names @cosmicdrift/kumiko-dev-server/testing. No code change.

title: compliance profile labels are English
detail: The labels of the built-in compliance profiles (eu-dsgvo, swiss-dsg, de-hr-dsgvo-hgb, minimal) were German in the English source; locale packages keep their option translations, and the compliance-profiles catalog now shows those translations instead of the raw source label. Authority names such as the de-hr authority contact stay as the authority calls itself.

title: Guides and screenshots for system check, inbound mail, billing and the 0.392 upgrade
detail: New guides system-check, inbound-mail, billing-plans-and-checkout and upgrading-to-0-392 with screenshots from the use-all-bundled and styleguide specs. security-defaults splits the row level security section and adds a scope diagram, a raw access example and crossTenantReads; handler-context-and-embedded-fields gets a namespace table; auth-external-login, prod-bootstrap, screen-layout, renderer-widget-options, rbac-tenant-isolation and cap-overview cover returnTo, static login, MFA policies, requiredEnvFor, jobs readRoles, header actions, screen gates, previewOpenByDefault, bulk actions, export and showLimit. New user guide operator-screens, and the sample index wires matrix screenshots into the feature reference previews of admin-shell, audit, jobs, cap-overview, tenant-settings, delivery, compliance-profiles, account-security and sessions. No framework code change.

title: events prune removes retired aggregate types from the event log
detail: `@cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/events-cli` exports `runEventsCli(argv, out, { features, rowLevelSecurity? })`. `events prune --aggregate-type <type> [--aggregate-type <type> ...]` reports events, aggregates and tenants per type; with `--apply` it deletes, in one transaction and in system scope, the events, snapshots, archive markers and dead letters of these types and empties the projections fed only by them. A projection that also reads other types makes the run refuse. Unknown or empty types fail without deleting anything. Use it when old events of a retired type break the rebuild of `schema apply`. Apps add `if (cmd === "events")` to `bin/kumiko.ts`; new scaffolds get it.

title: beforeTransactionWhenNested skip lets a handler with a beforeTransaction phase run nested
detail: `beforeTransactionWhenNested: "skip"` on a write handler lets a nested ctx.dispatch.write run it without the phase. `event.prepared` is then `undefined` (typed `TPrepared | undefined`) and the handler does that work inside its own transaction. Top-level commands still run the phase. Without the option a nested call stays rejected. Boot rejects the option without beforeTransaction and together with reserveBeforeTransaction; transaction "perCommand" is already rejected next to beforeTransaction.

title: KMS outages surface as EncryptionUnavailableError
detail: The PII key store configured with configurePiiSubjectKms wraps adapter failures (database, Key Manager, network) in EncryptionUnavailableError with code encryption_unavailable and HTTP status 503, exported from @cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/crypto together with ENCRYPTION_UNAVAILABLE_CODE. Key-state errors (KeyNotFoundError, KeyErasedError, KeyAlreadyExistsError) keep their types. Callers can tell an outage, which they retry later, from a problem with the record.

title: Live signals for entity names with uppercase runs reach the client
detail: `toKebab` now lives once in `@cosmicdrift/kumiko-types/kebab-case` and is used by the server read-access keys, the qualified-name helpers and the renderer. Before, the renderer and server copies could diverge for names like `aiURLCheck`, so a screen subscribed to a name the server never signalled. Boot now fails when two entities of different features fold to the same key (`billing.period` and `billingPeriod`), instead of merging their read rules.

title: Table and migration generation split into smaller steps
detail: fieldToColumnMeta, buildEntityTable and renderMigrationSql are now tables and named steps instead of long functions. Columns, indexes and migration SQL are byte-identical; nothing changes for apps.

title: requiredEnvFor reads a required env var in ops scripts
detail: @cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/env exports requiredEnvFor(label, env). It returns a reader that hands back the value of a set variable and throws "[label] required env var NAME is missing or empty" otherwise; an empty string counts as missing and the error never contains a value. The env source is passed in, so a script can read from the KEK-resolved env of resolvePlatformKeks as well as from process.env. It replaces the requiredEnv copies in app bin/ops scripts.

title: The boot validator checks header.statusFormat
detail: A projectionDetail screen with header.statusFormat but without header.status fails boot, because there is no badge to format.

title: The boot check validates inlineActions
detail: Every id in a projectionDetail inlineActions list must name a declared action (or edit when the screen has an edit target), the same rule as primaryAction; an unknown id fails the boot.

title: The i18n boot check covers emptyState variants
detail: Title and description keys of relatedList emptyState variants count as required surface keys, so a missing translation fails the boot check.

title: projectionDetail visibleWhen can pass the route id
detail: A screen-level visibleWhen takes idParam on projectionDetail. The gate then queries with the route id under that key, and boot accepts a visibleWhen query that requires exactly that input. Without idParam the empty-payload rule stays, and idParam on another screen type fails boot. A failing gate query, such as a 403 for a downgraded tenant, shows the fallback or the standard notice instead of the screen.

title: Boot errors name the real schema command
detail: The drift report and the row-level-security boot check recommended `kumiko schema apply` and `kumiko schema generate`. Apps run the CLI as `bun kumiko-schema <subcommand>`, so the hints now say that.

title: Concurrent boots create kumiko_es_operations without a race
detail: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS is not race-safe in Postgres, so replicas booting against a fresh database could fail on pg_type_typname_nsp_index. createEsOperationsTable now takes an advisory lock and checks again before it creates the table.

title: r.probe registers live readiness probes with a per-probe timeout
detail: A feature registers a probe with r.probe({ name, scope, cost, area, label, timeoutMs?, targets?, run }). scope "system" probes run only for SystemAdmins, "tenant" probes also for TenantAdmins of that tenant; cost "paid" probes run only when the caller asks for them. targets splits one probe into one result per target, such as one per mailbox. runWithTimeout from the api barrel is the shared timeout runner the readiness checks and probe runs use. A probe's context holds db, registry, obs, tz and services plus the run fields; the run job's dispatch, event emitter and escape-hatch powers stay with the job. The readiness status query still makes no network call.

title: The boot validator checks enumOption tones
detail: A list column with renderer { format: "enumOption", tones } fails boot when a tone is not one of the select-option tones.

title: Cloudflare is no longer listed as a sub-processor
detail: DNS moved to Hetzner, so Cloudflare, Inc. no longer processes data for the platform. The entry is gone from KUMIKO_SUB_PROCESSORS, which means it is missing from /api/compliance/sub-processors and from the sub-processor RSS feed.

title: schema apply in the production image uses the runtime's row-level security mode
detail: The app image ships only kumiko/migrations, not kumiko/schema.ts. Without the schema file `schema apply` ran with row-level security "off", so kumiko_events, kumiko_snapshots and kumiko_archived_streams were not healed and the boot of an app in "on" mode (the default) failed with "framework tables without it". Without a schema file apply now uses the same default as runProdApp. RunSchemaCliOptions takes an optional rowLevelSecurity, which wins over the schema file; the scaffolded bin/kumiko.ts passes appConfig.rowLevelSecurity, like bin/main.ts does for runProdApp. Apps that do not set rowLevelSecurity need no change. An app that sets rowLevelSecurity "off" and keeps a hand-written bin/kumiko.ts must pass rowLevelSecurity: "off" to runSchemaCli, otherwise apply enables row-level security on the framework tables and the app's "off" boot check fails.

title: Projection rebuilds no longer report drift on timestamptz columns
detail: Event payloads keep the microseconds of an instant, the live write stores milliseconds. A rebuild bound the payload's ISO string unchanged and wrote a different value, which the shadow diff reported as column drift. ISO instant strings bound to a timestamptz column are now truncated to milliseconds like Temporal.Instant values.

title: The live row-level security check of `kumiko check` covers only the app's own tables
detail: `schema validate` (the boot step of `kumiko check`) checks the live database when DATABASE_URL is set. On a dev database several apps share it failed on the other apps' tables. It now checks the tables kumiko/schema.ts declares plus the framework tables; tables no feature declares any more are still reported by the boot check, which runs against the app's own database. An unreachable database still fails the check.

title: kumiko-upgrade runs the codemods of its own feature-ast install
detail: The kumiko-upgrade bins of kumiko-cli and kumiko-dev-server now look for the codemod scripts from their own package first, so a feature-ast copy hoisted above the app (for example in a workspace parent) can no longer supply codemods of another version. runUpgradeCli takes an optional codemodResolveFrom for that; without it the search still starts at the repo root.

title: zod range moved to ^4.6.7
detail: All framework packages and the scaffold template require zod ^4.6.7, which fixes GHSA-MRHX-C7XC-M3W5.

title: Parallel writes in one handler no longer abort the transaction
detail: Bun.SQL does not serialize savepoints on a transaction. A handler that started several executor writes on ctx.db with Promise.all opened overlapping savepoints, the first RELEASE also released its neighbours, and the next one aborted the whole transaction with a 500. runInSavepoint and runInSavepointIfSupported now queue savepoints per transaction (proxy runners over the same transaction share one queue, savepoints opened from inside a running one still nest), and an executor verb on a handler transaction now runs in its own savepoint: when it fails, its event append, projection and hooks roll back together, also when the handler catches the failure, so no event without projection is left behind and a rebuild replays cleanly. Postgres errors 22007 and 22008 (a date or time value the column rejects, such as 2026-02-30) now map to a 400 validation_error instead of a 500, on writes and on query filters.

title: HandlerContext without wiring, hooks receive the HandlerContext
detail: HandlerContext has 19 members and no longer carries the AppContext wiring. ctx.services holds redis, cacheSync, jobRunner, searchAdapter, entityCache, secrets, kms, files, derivatives, configResolver, configEncryption, rateLimit, effectiveFeatures and masterKeyProvider; every key of an app's extraContext that the framework does not know now lives in ctx.services.extensions (it used to sit flat on the context through a spread, invisible to tsc). ctx.lifecycle holds afterCommit and afterRollback (replacing scheduleAfterCommit and scheduleAfterRollback), signal and runPreSave. ctx.tenants holds config (replacing configFor) and writeTarget (replacing forTenant). ctx.obs gains meter, and the flat log, tracer, _tenantId, systemUser and triggeredBy are gone; read ctx.user.tenantId and ctx.obs.log. JobContext no longer extends the shared wiring fields; it gets services and lifecycle.signal and keeps systemUser, triggeredBy and its job fields. All hooks (preSave, postSave, postSaveBatch, preDelete, postDelete, postDeleteBatch, preQuery, postQuery) and the system hook definitions receive the HandlerContext instead of the AppContext, and the batch hooks run on a real handler context built per flush. AppContext stays the flat boot wiring and declares services as never, so a handler or job context can no longer be passed to a function that takes an AppContext. The context of beforeTransaction no longer exposes ctx.systemDb.outsideTransaction, which was a hole next to the denied ctx.db.outsideTransaction. The member-resolution and pre-transaction contexts also drop the notify factories from ctx.services, and member resolution drops _fileProviderResolver, so neither can rebuild the denied notify or file storage. Helpers that took a structural context with an optional flat member read undefined once a handler context stopped carrying it; their shapes now make that a type error: requireSecretsContext, FileProviderContext (createFileProviderForTenant) and MailTransportContext (createTransportForTenant) take a required secrets key (handlers pass { secrets: ctx.services.secrets, user: ctx.user }), and CreateFileRefContext/UploadFileBytesContext read services.files, so a handler or job context passes straight in. bridgeStub accepts a services option.
migration: Run kumiko-upgrade --apply; it runs the ctx-namespaces codemod. It rewrites ctx.redis, cacheSync, jobRunner, searchAdapter, entityCache, secrets, kms, files, derivatives, configResolver, effectiveFeatures and the other service members to ctx.services.*, scheduleAfterCommit and scheduleAfterRollback to ctx.lifecycle.afterCommit and afterRollback, signal to ctx.lifecycle.signal, configFor and forTenant to ctx.tenants.config and writeTarget, and hook parameters annotated AppContext to HandlerContext, including context.log to context.obs.log in the hook body. Keys of your extraContext that you read through a cast move to ctx.services.extensions. Listed for manual review: ctx.systemUser, ctx.triggeredBy and ctx._tenantId on a HandlerContext (read ctx.user), a handler or job context passed to a function that takes an AppContext (narrow that parameter to the members it reads), spread literals next to moved members, and a handler or job context passed to a parameter whose structural type reads a moved member (it would read undefined without a type error). Hand-built test contexts take services, lifecycle and tenants from bridgeStub({ services }).

title: HandlerContext and JobContext use namespaces instead of flat members
detail: The roughly 40 flat members of HandlerContext are grouped by purpose, with no deprecated aliases. ctx.db.outsideTransaction replaces ctx.dbOutsideTransaction and ctx.outsideTransaction (the property is non-enumerable and sits on the same db object, so TenantDb identity stays intact; it is undefined in the member-resolution and before-transaction phases and in platform-metering tenant mode). ctx.events holds append, unsafeAppend, tryAppend, fetchForWriting, load, archive, restore, isArchived, snapshot and loadWithSnapshot. ctx.dispatch holds query, queryAs, write, writeAs, queryAsMember and queryProjection. ctx.auth holds resolveClaims and resolveActiveMembership. ctx.obs holds log, tracer, metrics and metricsFor, and ctx.obs.log is now always a Logger. JobContext gets the subsets events.append, dispatch.write/writeAs/queryAs/queryAsMember and obs.log/metricsFor. reserveBeforeTransaction and beforeTransaction receive the new ReservationContext and BeforeTransactionContext types, so the surfaces they deny no longer exist on the type. The deprecated _configAccessorFactory alias is removed; use configAccessorFactory. The cap-counter resolvers and the template-resolver PrepareContext now take ReservationContext instead of HandlerContext (type-level break for callers passing a full HandlerContext-typed value to a narrower position, and for wrappers declaring the old type). attachOutsideTransaction(db, outsideDb) from @cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/engine gives hand-built contexts a db.outsideTransaction; it mutates the passed db with a non-enumerable property (Object.defineProperty) and returns the same object. bridgeStub now accepts log and dispatch options. AppContext stays flat, and the context handed to postSave, preDelete, postDelete and postQuery hooks still reads context.log; a separate hook context follows in a later release.
migration: Run kumiko-upgrade --apply; it runs the ctx-namespaces codemod. It rewrites ctx.dbOutsideTransaction and ctx.outsideTransaction to ctx.db.outsideTransaction, ctx.appendEvent/unsafeAppendEvent/tryAppendEvent/fetchForWriting/loadAggregate/archiveStream/restoreStream/isStreamArchived/snapshotAggregate/loadAggregateWithSnapshot to ctx.events.append/unsafeAppend/tryAppend/fetchForWriting/load/archive/restore/isArchived/snapshot/loadWithSnapshot, ctx.query/queryAs/write/writeAs/queryAsMember/queryProjection to ctx.dispatch.*, ctx.resolveAuthClaims/resolveActiveMembership to ctx.auth.resolveClaims/resolveActiveMembership, and ctx.log/tracer/metrics/metricsFor to ctx.obs.*. Object literals typed as HandlerContext or JobContext (test mocks) are nested the same way. Sites the codemod cannot resolve are listed for manual review: spread literals, untyped receivers, and AppContext reads such as context.log in hooks, which stay as they are. Manual pattern { db: someDb, dbOutsideTransaction: x } becomes db: attachOutsideTransaction(someDb, x). Spread calls such as ...bridgeStub() next to moved members are reworked by hand; pass log/dispatch as bridgeStub options. Rename _configAccessorFactory to configAccessorFactory where you set it on an AppContext.

detail: Feature AST, pattern library and codemods moved to the new package @cosmicdrift/kumiko-feature-ast; kumiko-upgrade heals stale open lines in CHANGELOG.md

title: kumiko-upgrade --apply and --resolve heal stale open lines in CHANGELOG.md
migration: Every manual migration the upgrade marker lists as resolved gets its status in CHANGELOG.md, including `- [open]` lines in older sections left behind by a resolve with an older CLI.

title: allAppFeatures documents that its list is raw
detail: The JSDoc of allAppFeatures says the list has no bundled foundation and that tooling such as runSchemaCli takes FEATURES from kumiko/schema. Behavior is unchanged.

title: Jobs append their own events with ctx.events.append
detail: Jobs no longer need escapeHatch or unsafeRaw plus the low-level event-store API to append their own feature's events. The same ownership and schema rules apply as in write handlers, and the append runs in its own transaction together with the inline projections.
migration: JobContext has a new required field events.append. Code that builds a JobContext object by hand (boot seeds, test fixtures) and does not spread bridgeStub() adds an events.append that throws when the code under test never appends. Jobs that appended their own feature's events through escapeHatch or unsafeRaw switch to ctx.events.append({ type, aggregateId, aggregateType, payload }).

title: Jobs see whether they can still defer (ctx.canDefer)
detail: ctx.canDefer is false when the run is inline or the maxDefers budget is used up, so a handler can write its terminal state instead of deferring into an UnrecoverableError. Behaviour of ctx.defer and the maxDefers failure is unchanged.
migration: JobContext has a new required field canDefer. Code that builds a JobContext object by hand (boot seeds, test fixtures) adds `canDefer: false` unless the context really supports ctx.defer. Contexts built by the job runner or cast with `as unknown as JobContext` need no change.

title: meilisearch is an optional peer dependency
migration: Apps that import @cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/search/meilisearch add meilisearch to their own dependencies (bun add meilisearch@^0.58.0); without it that import fails at boot with a message that names the package. Apps without the Meilisearch adapter need nothing.

Names added since 0.389.0 stay public. 1236 names had no user and are removed from their subpath; 30 of them are deleted together with their code and tests, the rest stay inside the framework as internal modules without a public export. migration: None of the removed names had a user in any Kumiko repository, so no migration is expected. Internal names have no public replacement. The deleted names listed above are gone without a replacement; code that still imports one fails to compile and has to inline the few lines it needs. If you need one back, open an issue.

title: Job runner connects to a password-protected Redis
detail: parseRedisOpts kept only host, port and db of REDIS_URL, so BullMQ queues and the sequential lock connected without the password and the app stopped at boot with "Redis not reachable" against a Redis that requires auth. Username, URL-encoded password and rediss:// TLS are now carried over.

title: preQuery hooks removed
detail: `r.hook({ type: "preQuery", … })` registered a hook that the query pipeline never called. The `preQuery` hook type, `PreQueryHookFn`, the `preQuery` slot of the hook maps and registrar extension hooks, and `registry.getPreQueryHooks` are removed. A `type: "preQuery"` registration is now a type error and throws at feature registration instead of being silently ignored.
migration: No known users. Remove `r.hook({ type: "preQuery", … })` registrations; they never ran. To change a query payload, validate or transform it inside the query handler.

title: Row level security policy DDL behind a rowLevelSecurity parameter
detail: renderTableDdl, renderTablesDdl and unsafePushTables accept rowLevelSecurity "off" or "on" (default "off", output unchanged). With "on", every table that has a tenant_id column gets ENABLE and FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY plus the policies kumiko_tenant_isolation and kumiko_system_tenant_read, driven by the kumiko.tenant_id and kumiko.scope settings. Tables without tenant_id are left alone.

title: The migration generator writes a row level security section
detail: With rowLevelSecurity "on", generateMigration adds a Row level security section for new, changed and recreated tables and a rowLevelSecurity field to the snapshot; switching back to "off" emits the matching DISABLE statements with a warning. Without the option the generated SQL and snapshot are byte-identical to before.

title: Migration replay understands CREATE, ALTER and DROP POLICY
detail: The replay behind kumiko-schema validate tracks ENABLE and FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY and policy definitions per table, follows table renames, and reports row-level-security-drift when the committed SQL does not produce the policies the snapshot expects (missing, extra, altered or hand-edited) or turns on row level security for a table the snapshot has no spec for. An unparsable policy statement, or a policy or row level security change inside a DO block, fails loudly.

title: Projection and multi-stream rebuilds no longer abort on tables with row level security
detail: The shadow swap used to refuse a live table with RLS flags or policies. It now reads them from the catalog under the swap lock, re-applies them to the swapped-in table and fails the rebuild transaction if the result differs. Before the first read, the rebuild checks that the table's policies let its system scope see every row, so the guards never see too few rows and the swap never drops hidden ones.

title: Migration replay parses ALTER TABLE ONLY, IF EXISTS and public. prefixes
detail: kumiko-schema validate read `ALTER TABLE ONLY "t"` as a change to a table named ONLY and ignored IF EXISTS and a public. prefix; the statement now applies to the named table.

title: createTenantDb mode system requires a reason
detail: The system scope a TenantDb opens for its statements now carries that reason, so a scope leak assertion names the call site. Tenant mode takes no reason.
migration: Add `reason: "<why this access spans tenants>"` to every createTenantDb({ mode: "system" }) call. The reason must be a non-empty string literal: an empty reason throws InternalError at construction, and the internal-subpath-imports guard rejects a missing, empty or non-literal reason.

title: Signature routes read and write secrets in a system scope
detail: With row level security on, verify() and the handler of a signature route (subscription webhooks, mail connect callbacks) read the secrets of a tenant named by the signed request before any tenant scope exists, and failed. deps.secrets now opens the system scope for each secret access only, so plugin code that parses the unauthenticated body stays unscoped.

title: RLS boot check tells known tables from orphaned ones
detail: With rowLevelSecurity on, the boot check lists tenant tables without row-level security in two groups. Tables the app schema knows point to kumiko schema generate. Tables no feature declares anymore, including retired framework tables, are named as orphaned and point to dropping them by migration. The check itself stays strict.
migration: assertRowLevelSecurityBootState takes the known tables as a required third argument: pass knownTablesOf(features), both exported from the db subpath.

title: schema apply heals row-level security on existing framework tables
detail: Existing databases got no policies on kumiko_events, kumiko_archived_streams and kumiko_snapshots, so boot failed while schema validate stayed green.

title: Connections set the row level security scope in every transaction
detail: createDbConnection takes rowLevelSecurity "off" or "on" (default "off", the connection is unchanged). With "on", every statement and transaction sets kumiko.tenant_id and kumiko.scope transaction-locally from the ambient scope. TenantDb sets its tenant, and the system scope for system-mode TenantDbs, global tables and a granted unsafeRaw. Dispatch sets the user's tenant per command, or the system scope for a system-scoped handler. Event store reads and writes use the stream's tenant. Jobs, the event dispatcher, member resolution, migrations, boot seeds, retention, reindex, blind-index cleanup, the PII backfill, projection apply, auth providers and the tenant lifecycle check run in system scope. A statement without a scope sees no tenant rows. The functions that set a scope (runInRowLevelSecurityScope, runInSystemRowLevelSecurityScope, tenantRowLevelSecurityScope, systemScopedRunner) are not part of the public db subpath; framework packages import them from @cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/internal/row-level-security, which no guard closes to apps yet. App code reaches the system scope through a system-scoped handler, a job or a granted unsafeRaw.

title: One rowLevelSecurity value in kumiko.config.ts for schema tooling and runners
detail: AppConfig.rowLevelSecurity ("off" by default) is exported by the managed kumiko/schema.ts as ROW_LEVEL_SECURITY. kumiko-schema generate and validate render and check the policies from it, and apply opens its connection in that mode; the CLI has no flag of its own. The API, worker and all-in-one entrypoints take the same option and refuse a context whose connection runs in another mode. unsafePushTables with "on" reads the catalog first and runs no lock and no DDL for a table that already has ENABLE, FORCE and both kumiko policies.

title: Projection rebuilds run in system scope under row level security
detail: The rebuild transaction no longer turns row_security off, so a rebuild works as a NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS table owner under FORCE. Before the first guard read it locks the live table in SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE mode, which blocks policy DDL and a second rebuild of the same table, and reads the catalog. When row level security is enabled, kumiko_tenant_isolation must exist as a PERMISSIVE policy for ALL commands and PUBLIC and no RESTRICTIVE policy may exist; otherwise the rebuild fails with the table and its policies and leaves the live table untouched. Other permissive policies carry over to the swapped-in table. Multi-stream rebuilds follow the same rule.

title: rowLevelSecurity defaults to "on"
detail: Postgres row level security is on by default, system scopes carry a mandatory reason, and the event write path keeps the caller's tenant scope.
migration:
In the app repo, once with the bump: run `kumiko sync-managed --write` (the managed kumiko/schema.ts now reads `export const ROW_LEVEL_SECURITY = appConfig.rowLevelSecurity;`), then `kumiko schema generate` and commit the migration. It contains ENABLE and FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY plus the policies `kumiko_tenant_isolation` and `kumiko_system_tenant_read` for every tenant table. The schema apply (the migrate init container in production) creates them; there is no manual database step. Without the migration, boot at "on" refuses to start and names the unprotected tables.
The app's database role must not skip policies; boot refuses it otherwise. Check it as that role with `SELECT rolsuper, rolbypassrls FROM pg_roles WHERE rolname = current_user` (both must be false). Callers of createDbConnection without a mode now get "on"; tools that touch no tenant rows (schema baseline/status, the KMS key store) pass "off" explicitly, and the operator commands backfill-pii, waitlist-migrate, project and consumer run on an enforcing connection in system scope, so they work against both modes.
Way back: set `rowLevelSecurity: "off"` in kumiko.config.ts and run `kumiko schema generate`; the generated migration contains DISABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY and drops the policies. At "off" runProdApp and runWorkerApp log a boot warning.

title: Boot hooks with a db dependency get a system-scoped db at rowLevelSecurity "on"
migration: No action unless a hook relied on the unscoped pool. The anonymousAccess factory, enrichAnonymousAccess, the runProdApp `wire` hook and runWorkerApp `wireComponents` now receive a system-scoped db, the same in prod, dev and the test stack, so tenant resolution and boot reads see rows across tenants. Anything the anonymousAccess factory builds keeps that db at request time and therefore reads across tenants for anonymous callers: filter by the resolved tenant yourself. In prod, extraContext factories keep the ambient request scope; the test stack and dev still hand them a system-scoped db, so a service that needs cross-tenant reads at request time must scope itself.

title: runInSystemRowLevelSecurityScope and systemScopedRunner take a reason
migration: Call runInSystemRowLevelSecurityScope("<why this access spans tenants>", fn) and systemScopedRunner(runner, "<reason>"). An empty or whitespace reason throws InternalError; the scope leak assertion names the reason.

title: A projection write under a tenant scope can no longer land in another tenant
detail: applyEntityEvent keeps an ambient tenant scope instead of wrapping every write in a system scope. Writes for other tenants go through ctx.systemDb.acknowledgeCrossTenant in an r.systemScope() feature. Replays, rebuilds and global entities still write system scoped.
migration: A command that writes an entity row for another tenant through ctx.db now fails with SQLSTATE 42501; move that write to ctx.systemDb.acknowledgeCrossTenant in an r.systemScope() feature.

title: composeFeatures no longer warns about its own bundled copies
detail: Composing the output of a first composeFeatures pass again drops the earlier bundled instances silently; only copies the app supplied itself still warn.

title: Scoped pool statements pipeline their transaction
detail: A pool statement under a row level security scope sends BEGIN, the transaction-local scope, the statement and COMMIT pipelined on one reserved connection instead of waiting for each, which cuts its roundtrips roughly in half. The connection returns to the pool only after COMMIT settled.

title: Schema generator emits primary-key changes
detail: A changed primary key (single to composite, reordered columns, renamed constraint) previously produced no migration. The generator now emits DROP CONSTRAINT plus ADD CONSTRAINT with a WARN comment, and managed projections are recreated and replayed.

title: Tests seed and reset event-sourced tables through the event store
detail: Seeds of user, membership, tenant and other entity rows use seedRowViaEventStore instead of seedRow, so their created events exist. Setup and teardown hooks in the integration tests clear event-sourced tables through resetTestTables instead of raw DELETE statements, and clear the events table in the same call, so a test no longer starts with events whose projection rows are gone. Nothing changes for apps; the packages are only republished.

title: Bun.SQL replaces postgres-js as the only Postgres driver
detail: createDbConnection opens a Bun.SQL pool and needs Bun 1.4.4 or newer, the first release that drops a cached statement plan after DDL on the same connection. The handle gains listenClient for LISTEN/NOTIFY. Server errors carry the code ERR_POSTGRES_SERVER_ERROR with the SQLSTATE in errno and the constraint name in constraint; connection failures carry ERR_POSTGRES_CONNECTION_CLOSED, ERR_POSTGRES_CONNECTION_REFUSED, ERR_POSTGRES_CONNECTION_TIMEOUT or ERR_POSTGRES_CONNECTION_FAILED. extractPgError, isUniqueViolation, isTableAlreadyExists, constraintOf and the newly exported isUndefinedTable read that shape. The onNotice option is removed, because Bun.SQL has no notice hook and drops server notices. The ssl option takes Bun's tls value (a boolean, "disable", "prefer", "require", "verify-ca", "verify-full" or a TLS options object); ssl true and a TLS object without rejectUnauthorized still verify the server certificate, as they did with postgres-js. DB_PROVIDER is refused at boot for every non-empty value, "postgres" included.
migration: Read SQLSTATE and constraint only through extractPgError or the is* helpers from @cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/db; a direct err.code === "23505" check or an err.constraint_name read no longer matches. Replace checks for CONNECTION_CLOSED, CONNECTION_ENDED, CONNECTION_DESTROYED or CONNECT_TIMEOUT with the ERR_POSTGRES_CONNECTION_* codes. Drop onNotice from createDbConnection calls. Remove DB_PROVIDER from every environment. Run on Bun 1.4.4 or newer in engines, CI and images. Code that imports postgres itself must declare its own dependency or move to Bun.SQL, since the framework no longer installs it. Manual migration, there is no codemod.

title: schema status and baseline use one connection, bun-types is a peer dependency
detail: kumiko schema status and baseline open a pool of one connection instead of the default size, because Bun.SQL dials every pool connection on the first query. bun-types is now a peer dependency (^1.4.4) of framework, types, server-runtime and dev-server instead of a regular dependency, so install it next to the framework.

title: validateBundledListsOptions and the BundledListsOptions type
detail: BundledListsOptions is exported from the types package and the engine barrel. validateBundledListsOptions rejects unknown keys, grouping, totals and pinFirstColumn without table.pinning with a message that names the key, and checks the remaining keys like a screen's own table block.

title: r.adoptsBundledLists() marks features that take the bundledLists block
detail: The registrar method r.adoptsBundledLists() marks a feature whose list screens take the app-wide bundledLists block; the flag appears as FeatureDefinition.adoptsBundledLists and in feature-manifest.json, and the feature-ast parser knows the call as an opaque singleton pattern.

title: table block on entityList, projectionList and relatedList
detail: The new optional table block (rememberState, resetAll, columnPicker, density with default and userChoice) is validated at boot; unknown keys, hidden columns without columnPicker and invalid density values are rejected. Columns accept hidden: true. Remembered state lives in sessionStorage per tenant and user and is cleared on logout or identity change.

title: table.pinning, table.resizing and table.keyboardNavigation, column pinned, width and minWidth
detail: The boot validator rejects pinned without table.pinning, a pinned value other than left or right, width or minWidth without table.resizing, values that are not finite numbers above 0, and a minWidth above the width.

title: Money list aggregates answer one value per currency
detail: A sum, avg, min or max measure over a money field in a list aggregate now answers [{ currency, value }] with value in minor units, one entry per currency in the matching rows, and never adds amounts of different currencies. Before, it answered one plain number over all currencies.
migration: code reading measures of a money field from a list aggregate answer (executor.aggregate, answerListAggregate or the list query with aggregate) reads an array of { currency, value } instead of a number; take the entry of the wanted currency, value stays in minor units

title: table.grouping, table.totals and range facets validated at boot
detail: The table block takes grouping ({ field, label?, labels?, collapsedWhen?, userChoice?, fields? }) and totals ([{ field, kind }]). The boot validator checks the fields against the entity or the columns, rejects measures a field type cannot carry and requires the list query to accept aggregate (entityListSchema does; hand-written queries answer it with answerListAggregate). facets.<field>.display "range" needs a filterable number, decimal, money or bigInt field.

title: bulkActions on entityList, projectionList and relatedList
detail: Each entry is { id, rowAction, confirm? } and points at a writeHandler entry of the same screen's rowActions. The boot validator rejects unknown keys, a non-kebab or duplicate id, an unknown rowAction and a rowAction of kind clientAction, navigate or drawer.

title: XLSX export for entityList and projectionList via table.export
detail: The new table.export block ({ xlsx: true, maxRows? }) is validated at boot and is only accepted on entityList and projectionList. POST /api/export/xlsx runs the list query again with the caller's session, pages through the whole filtered list and answers 413 above maxRows (default 10000, hard cap 100000). Encrypted, sensitive, write-only and unreadable fields and virtual columns are left out of the sheet. Reference columns export the label of the target (joined with commas for multiple references), not the id. Timestamp cells use the browser time zone sent with the request, else the profile zone, else UTC. Personal access tokens are rejected. A projectionList query must honor offset or return nextCursor. Adds the write-excel-file dependency.

title: Executor writes on a pool runner are atomic
detail: executor.create/update/delete/forget/restore on a TenantDb that is not inside a transaction used to run append, projection and custom projections as separate autocommit statements, so a failing projection left an event without its row. They now run in their own transaction, and a returned failure such as version_conflict rolls it back too. Calls inside a handler transaction keep their savepoint behavior. Callers that wrapped executor writes in runInOwnTransaction as a workaround can drop it.

title: FeatureRegistrar types moved to @cosmicdrift/kumiko-types/feature-registrar
migration: Import FeatureRegistrar, HookDefinition, EntityObjectDefinition and RequiresApi from @cosmicdrift/kumiko-types/feature-registrar or from the engine barrel of @cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework; @cosmicdrift/kumiko-types/feature no longer exports them.

title: maxPerTenant counts active and waiting jobs in one snapshot
detail: The guard read the active and the waiting list with separate Redis calls, so a job that moved from waiting to active between them was missing from both and a dispatch over the cap got through. It now reads both lists with one getJobs snapshot per queue. The integration tests hold the cap jobs on a release gate instead of sleeping.

title: relatedList groupBy replaced by table.grouping
detail: The groupBy key on a relatedList section and an entityList expandableRow is removed together with the RelatedListGroupBy type. Both group through table.grouping ({ field, label?, labels?, collapsedWhen? }): groups, counts and header measures come from one aggregate query over all matching rows instead of the loaded page, and each open group loads its own rows. An expandableRow takes only table.grouping with a fixed field; userChoice, fields and every other table option stay boot errors there. The boot validator reports a leftover groupBy with a pointer to table.grouping. ExpandableRowGrouping is the new type of an expandableRow's grouping.
migration: move groupBy { field, collapsedWhen, label, labels } to table: { grouping: { field, collapsedWhen, label, labels } }; the bound query must accept aggregate (entityListSchema does, a hand-written query answers it with answerListAggregate). dateField and the {lastDate} placeholder have no replacement on an expandableRow, where totals stay off; on a relatedList a max measure in table.totals shows the latest date. Every group now gets a header: a group without label or labels entry shows its value instead of rendering headerless.

title: ctx.loadAggregate can read a single event by version
detail: The new atVersion option returns the event at that version of the stream (or nothing), with upcasting and the tenant filter. It cannot be combined with asOf. Workflow resume uses it for event references.

title: Access invalidation survives a Redis outage
detail: The consumer that pushes session, token and membership revocations to open streams does not count failed publishes towards the attempt limit and backs off between them, instead of dying after 10 failed deliveries and silently dropping later revocations. Other failures keep the limit. New EventConsumerErrorPolicy.isTransientError.

title: file upload rechecks the record lock when inserting the row
detail: POST /files with an entityId reads the stored row again through the inserting transaction and refuses with 409 record_locked when lockedWhen holds. The window between that read and the commit stays open, like for any other write that checks the lock before its own commit.

title: Meilisearch default upgrade cannot tell a narrowed configure() from an older default
detail: A tenant that called configure() with a strict subset of the default attributes gets the full default back after the next process restart, because Meilisearch stores no marker for an explicit configure(). Configure the full attribute set, or a set that contains an attribute outside the default, to keep it.

title: Cross-tenant-read crons audit once per day, not once per foreign row
detail: The process dedup key of a declared system cron hatch includes the target only for global-write (a table). Row targets of cross-tenant-read no longer grow the in-memory map or write one audit event per row.

title: Failed job-runner start waits for the timed-out boot gate
detail: start() now waits a bounded time for an abandoned boot gate before throwing, instead of leaving that to stop(). The scheduler-seen timer is only started after every step that can fail, so no timer outlives a failed start.

title: disabled feature no longer removes another feature's workspace with the same id
detail: buildAppSchema records which feature owns each workspace and the feature strip removes only the workspaces of the disabled features. Two features that use the same short workspace id keep their own entries.

title: upload ledger uses the injected clock
detail: createFileUploadLedger and withUploadLedger take an optional now function, and the file provider resolver wires AppContext.clock into it. Without a clock the system time is used as before.

title: anonymous save leaves foreign pending uploads unbound
detail: Integration test through the real write route with anonymous access, covering the save pipeline path of the pending-upload ownership check.

title: Unused ProviderPluginContext helpers removed
detail: ProviderPluginContext, providerPluginContextFromHandler and providerPluginContextFromJob are gone. No plugin type or resolver used them, and the type exposed db handles without an audit user. Provider contexts stay the narrow FileProviderContext, MailTransportContext and InboundMailContext.
migration: no known callers; use FileProviderContext, MailTransportContext or InboundMailContext

title: provider selector option labels are unique per owner
detail: The selector field id of a provider form is qualified with its owner feature, so the translation keys of its option labels change.
migration: move app translation overrides from config:entity:__config-edit__:field:provider:option:<value> to the owner-qualified field id, field:mail-foundation-provider:option:<value> or field:file-foundation-provider:option:<value>

title: live signals hide row ids from row-filtered roles
detail: createSseRoute takes an optional entityRowReadMaps option, built from entity access.read by the server routes. A signed-in connection receives id and version only if the entity has no read ownership map or one of its roles is mapped to all; otherwise the signal carries just the entity and event type so the client refetches.

title: write handlers that spread the executor result keep projections and postSave hooks
detail: The event is stripped from lifecycle results when the dispatcher masks the response, no longer made non-enumerable on the result, so copying the result does not lose it. Responses still carry no event.

title: event-free write results proven for non-HTTP entry points
detail: Integration tests assert that dispatcher.write, dispatcher.batch and the agent tool dispatch return no event. No runtime change: all of them already pass through the dispatcher masking.

title: reference-data seed adopts rows that have no event stream
detail: Rows from installs that seeded reference data by direct insert are re-created under the same id through the executor on the next boot, so updates apply and the rows survive a rebuild. No action is needed; the row id is unchanged, only its version restarts at 1.

title: client-errors route keeps an in-memory floor limit
detail: The in-memory per-IP limiter now runs in front of the Redis-backed limiter instead of only when no resolver is wired, so a failing resolver can no longer lift the limit on the public client-errors endpoint.

title: reindex job batches are no longer cut off by the server statement timeout
detail: reindexEntity reads each batch in its own transaction with statement_timeout lifted for that transaction, on the caller's own runner, so the job path through ctx.systemDb.unsafeRaw() keeps its gates.

title: files meta batch route is rate limited by id count
detail: createFileRoutes takes an optional metaBatchRateLimitResolver, wired by the server from the rate-limit resolver or Redis. A user over 1000 requested ids per minute gets 429 rate_limited; a failing limiter fails open and is reported like the other limiters.

title: kumiko-upgrade explains that --apply writes the CHANGELOG
detail: The preview run never wrote the upgrade CHANGELOG or the marker, and consumers running it without --apply got no entry and no explanation. It now prints a hint; the exit code is unchanged.

title: Codemod imports no longer land inside header comments
detail: ensureNamedImport appends the new import after the last existing import, so a file with a header comment block keeps the comment intact.

title: Database now is rounded to milliseconds
detail: The Postgres clock read behind readDatabaseNow is cast to timestamptz(3), the precision of events.created_at, so a comparison with a stored event time is exact.

title: E2E seeders and signature routes can write with explicit roles
detail: dispatchWriteAs on signature route deps and writeAs on the E2E seeder context run a write as the tenant's system user with the "system" role plus the given roles, without SystemAdmin. write() keeps running as SystemAdmin.

title: List filter on multiple references matches array contents
detail: eq, ne and in on a multi-reference field now check jsonb containment instead of scalar equality, and screen filters on such fields allow the equality operators. Consumers no longer need a full scan.

title: kumiko-upgrade --resolve updates CHANGELOG.md
detail: The Manual migrations lines of every CHANGELOG.md section change from [open] to the chosen resolution for the resolved ids; other entries and files without a CHANGELOG.md are left alone.

title: ctx.scheduleAfterRollback for outside-transaction compensation
detail: ctx.scheduleAfterRollback(fn) runs fn when the handler transaction does not commit, or when the enclosing savepoint of a nested ctx.write rolls back (after the outer transaction ends). It never runs on commit, errors are logged and do not change the write result, and it is absent outside a transaction scope (perCommand, post-commit, beforeTransaction, member resolution). A failed COMMIT also triggers it, so callbacks must be idempotent and outcome-safe, for example releasing a reservation row that may already be gone.

title: Tenant-safe upsert on ctx.db
detail: ctx.db.upsert(table, values, { conflictTarget, update? }) requires tenantId in conflictTarget and the target to match a declared unique index or primary key. The update only touches the row of the inserted tenant, update may not set tenantId, and the default update leaves conflict, primary-key and tenant columns alone. Event-fed tables are rejected. Replaces unsafeRaw plus upsertOnConflict for tenant-scoped upserts.

title: runProdApp passes errorDocs and instanceId to the server
detail: ApiEntrypointOptions now carries errorDocs and instanceId and createApiEntrypoint forwards them to the server. Before, runProdApp dropped its errorDocs option, and a KUMIKO_INSTANCE_ID set only in a custom envSource never reached the server, which fell back to process.env. The boot-abort cleanup of runProdApp also moved into a helper that swallows synchronously throwing cleanups.

title: Physical-table collisions use the DDL table name
detail: createRegistry compared entity tables under a feature-prefixed name that no DDL path creates, so an entity whose explicit table equals another feature's derived table name, or two entities with the same explicit table in different features, registered fine and then emitted the same CREATE TABLE twice. The check now uses the unprefixed physical name, the same as the store-table check and the migrate runner.
migration: Apps where two entities share a physical table name fail at boot with "has physical table ... which collides with entity ...". Give one of them a different `table`.

title: Worker entrypoint takes instanceId
detail: WorkerEntrypointOptions now carries instanceId (moved to BaseEntrypointOptions, so the API and all-in-one options keep it) and createWorkerEntrypoint forwards it to the server. runWorkerApp reads KUMIKO_INSTANCE_ID from its envSource like runProdApp, so with KUMIKO_INSTANCE_ID set, per-instance consumers in the worker and its app.started event use the same id. Before, the worker server only saw process.env.

title: PII, retention and cascade-delete rules as tables, English dev messages
detail: validatePiiAndRetention runs one checker per rule in a fixed order, and the cascade-delete hook dispatches each relation through a table of onDelete strategies. Error and warning texts, their order, transaction boundaries and event order are unchanged. buildAppSchema forwards field properties through an ordered table, and kumiko-upgrade and the pii-personal-migration codemod run one function per step; their output is byte-identical. The dev warnings of normalizeListColumn and buildAppSchema are now English.

title: Named steps for list reads, field columns, table metadata and table diffs
detail: The list read verb runs search, sort, cursor boundary, filters, stream-version projection, row rehydration and the next cursor as named steps in their own files next to event-store-executor-read.ts, and detail() shares the ownership and row rehydration steps. Field columns come from one emitter per field type in a typed table, so a new field type fails the typecheck until it has an emitter, and an unknown type from untyped input still throws "unhandled field type". deriveEntityTableMeta collects columns, foreign-key, blind-index and declared indexes in separate steps with the same overloads and error texts. diffOneTable compares columns and indexes through one comparator per kind and keeps the order of added, dropped and changed entries.

title: Per-kind tables for feature-AST id matching, editability and rendering
detail: callMatchesId() looks up one matcher per PatternId kind in a typed table in feature-ast/pattern-id-matchers.ts next to patch.ts. getEditability() reads a table keyed by pattern kind, and renderPattern() dispatches through one renderer per pattern kind. All three tables are typed over their kind union, so a new kind does not compile until it has an entry. The feature-ast barrel exports the same names as before.

title: Boot enforces the projection allowlist
detail: The projection allowlist validator existed but was never called from validateBoot. It now runs as the last cross-feature check. It also keys aggregate tables by the physical table name (entity.table or the derived read_* name) instead of the entity name, so unsafeProjection steps on the table of an entity without an explicit table, and duplicate tables between a derived and an explicit name, are detected.
migration: Apps with such violations fail at boot. Add the missing r.requires.projection or r.requires.step declaration, or use r.step.aggregate.* for aggregate tables.

title: Recipe for Input kind "code" in a confirmation step
detail: samples/recipes/auth-mfa has a ConfirmationCodeStep for e-mail or invite codes that uses Input kind "code" with length, autoFocus and onComplete, clears and refocuses after a rejected code, and has a DOM test. The agent example for auth-mfa includes it.

title: Groups and sums on the entity list query
detail: Pass aggregate with an optional groupBy field and up to 20 measures (sum, avg, count, min, max per field) to a list query. The answer is groups with key, count, one value per measure in request order and, for a reference groupBy, the label of the referenced row. Screen filters, search, ownership and field read access apply exactly as for rows; a field the caller may not read yields null or no groups, and encrypted, personal or secret fields and unsuitable field types are rejected with a validation error. At most 200 groups are returned, with truncated set beyond that. Custom query handlers use executor.aggregate or answerListAggregate.

title: buildServer split into middleware installers and route mounters
detail: buildServer() keeps its signature and behavior. Boot checks, pre-app wiring, the event dispatcher, middleware installers and route mounters now live in server-*.ts files next to server.ts. withFileProviderResolver and makeDispatchSystemWrite/makeDispatchWriteAs/makeDispatchSystemQuery are still exported from the api barrel under the same names.

title: Where-clause emitters, coercer table and named write steps
detail: buildWhereClause() now dispatches through one emitter per WhereOperator key in a typed table, and coerceDriverRow() looks up one coercer per pgType. Table introspection, value preparation, row coercion, closed-connection handling and aggregate SQL live in their own files next to db/query.ts. The create and update write verbs run preSave, field and ownership checks, the record-lock guard, select-option checks, the version check, the append and the projection as named steps. The db barrel exports the same names as before.

title: Job runner run path split into named steps
detail: handleJob() in jobs/job-runner.ts now composes the perTenant fan-out, the unknown-job check, the maxPerTenant defer gate and the sequential lock (job-runner-gates.ts), the run context with its db, service and dispatch facets (job-runner-context.ts), the job.execute span with success and failure recording (job-runner-execution.ts) and the handler deferral. The runner's shared state travels in one scope object (job-runner-scope.ts). The jobs barrel exports the same names as before. New integration tests cover unknown jobs taken from the queue, a perTenant wrapper for an unknown job, a perTenant job without a tenant resolver and ctx.defer with a non-positive delay.

title: Handler context and write pipeline split into named steps
detail: buildHandlerContext() in pipeline/dispatch-shared.ts now composes one builder per facet of the flat HandlerContext: the shared scope (handler-context-scope.ts), the tenant-scoped db handles, forTenant and file contexts (handler-context-db.ts), the commit sinks with ctx.query/write/queryAs/writeAs and nested writes in savepoints (handler-context-dispatch.ts), ctx.notify (handler-context-notify.ts), config, configFor, tz and locale (handler-context-config.ts), the event store surfaces and ctx.queryProjection (handler-context-events.ts), the identity-gated auth surfaces and ctx.hasFeature (handler-context-auth.ts) and log, tracer and metrics (handler-context-observability.ts). executeWriteInner() in pipeline/dispatch-write.ts runs the entry checks, the pre-handler gates with the reservation, the transition guard, the handler call and the settle step with reservation confirm, lifecycle and after-commit hooks as separate functions; executeNestedWrite() checks the nested foreign keys, verifies the parent row and writes the children in their own steps. Public exports are unchanged. New tests cover the ctx.snapshotAggregate/ctx.loadAggregateWithSnapshot roundtrip with tenant isolation and the no-database error text of the event store surfaces.

title: kumiko-schema output in English, schema CLI and screen key collection split per kind
detail: Visible change: kumiko-schema (and the dev `kumiko schema` command) now prints "is missing", "App convention", "No schema changes detected — no new migration file written.", "Review, hand-edit if needed, then git add + commit.", "is missing — run schema generate <name> first.", "No kumiko/migrations/ — the app is still on the legacy drizzle path.", "Unknown subcommand" / "Allowed", "must declare `export const ENTITY_METAS: EntityTableMeta[]`" and an English help text instead of the German lines. The standalone `kumiko schema apply` of production bundles prints "Creating framework infrastructure tables (idempotent)…", "Applying kumiko migrations (…)…", "… is missing — kumiko/migrations/ must be part of the image." and "Unknown command: kumiko … / The standalone bundle only supports 'kumiko schema apply'.". Scripts that matched the German text need the English one. Exit codes, the order of the output lines and which lines go to stderr are unchanged. runSchemaCli() keeps its signature; each subcommand lives in its own file under schema-cli/. requiredKeysFromScreen() returns the same keys in the same order; a screen with an unknown type (only reachable through a cast) yields just its title key.

title: validateScreens split into one validator per screen kind
detail: validateScreens() keeps its signature, its error messages and the order in which it reports the first error. The per-kind validators live in screens-kind-*.ts next to screens.ts, and checks shared by several kinds (empty columns or sections, header actions, write-handler registration) live in screens-kind-shared.ts and screens-actions.ts. A screen whose type is not a known kind now fails boot with an explicit "unknown type" error.

title: Sequential job lock released when run setup fails
detail: handleJob() claimed the sequential lock before prepareJobRun() and the onJobStart hook, but only released it in the finally block that started after them. A throwing onJobStart left the lock until its TTL (305 s) and every further invocation of that job was requeued behind it. Both calls now run inside the try and the lock is released by job name. A failure there is logged and, on the final attempt, reported through onJobFailed. The seed-migration failure message starts with systemWriteAs(...) instead of the duplicated [es-ops/seed-migration] prefix.

title: Reconnect after an outage no longer waits out connect_timeout
detail: The postgres.js fork left the write buffer of a dead socket in place, so the first query after a database outage queued its startup message behind stale bytes and failed with CONNECT_TIMEOUT after 30 seconds. The fork now resets the buffer when the socket closes, and the next query opens a fresh connection immediately.

title: rateLimitCost for write handlers
detail: A write handler can declare `rateLimitCost: (payload) => number`. The result is booked on every declared `rateLimit` bucket instead of the options' static `cost`; values below 1 count as 1 and non-finite values fail the request. The bucket is charged after schema validation, so an invalid payload costs nothing, and a rejected request consumes no tokens. Boot fails when `rateLimitCost` is set without an active `rateLimit`, or on an anonymous or ip-limited handler, because the cost books after the parse and such a handler would lose its pre-parse protection.
migration: Optional. Bulk handlers should add `rateLimitCost: (p) => p.files.length` so a request with many items is not counted as one.

title: Codemods no longer drop side-effect imports or miss moved index files
detail: The testing-move codemod repoints side-effect and empty imports instead of deleting them. The feature-layout codemod rewrites directory imports such as "./components" when the moved file is components/index.ts.

title: Review fixes for notify, form derivations, i18n keys, feature AST, nav stripping and escape-hatch audit
detail: A deferred ctx.notify with Temporal values in data no longer fails the write. Form derivations take the literal currency or the source currency before the client value, reject mixed-currency operands, and the boot validator now rejects derive definitions that mix money with number/decimal units or use non-numeric sources. Metric labels of projectionDetail screens are required i18n keys. The feature AST keeps backingTable on spread entity definitions. Pure grouping navs emptied by disabled features are removed. db.global() writes are audited per table.

title: Client-error rate limit survives address rotation
detail: Without Redis, the per-process limiter now drops the least recently seen IPs when more than 10000 are tracked, so a flood of fresh addresses no longer resets the window of every other IP.

title: Stalled SSE clients are dropped without further broadcasts
detail: The heartbeat ping is written and tracked like entity frames instead of awaited, so a client that stopped reading is aborted at the next heartbeat after the stall timeout and releases its broker slot.

title: Leftover __Host- cookies are expired with secureCookies:false too
detail: Clearing the session cookies now always sends the Secure delete for the __Host- auth and csrf variants when the configured names are unprefixed, so an app switched to secureCookies:false behind a TLS proxy no longer keeps a stale __Host- csrf cookie.

title: runAsDirectCallEntry renamed to runAsAgentToolCallEntry
detail: The internal request-context helper also marks its scope as an agent tool call, so the name now says so; it stays reserved for dispatchToolCall.
migration: replace imports of runAsDirectCallEntry from @cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/internal/request-context with runAsAgentToolCallEntry; the signature is unchanged

title: Version conflicts skip the extra stream-version lookup
detail: The CRUD executor reports the current version carried by the event store conflict and queries the stream again only when the conflict carries none.

title: distinctOn documents that system reference rows compete for newest
detail: The tenant-scoped read set includes system reference rows, so they take part in the newest-row pick; the docs name the tenantId filter that restricts it to own rows, and tests pin both behaviours. Tests also cover the createDbConnection ssl and onNotice options, the version-conflict race over HTTP, and the advisory-lock waiter probe is scoped to its own lock.

title: Empty and exclusion tenant filters no longer widen a read
detail: A where.tenantId of { in: [] } now returns no rows, and { ne } or { notIn } keep excluding the named tenants instead of falling back to the caller's full scope. scopeTenantDbToTenant keeps the write denial of its source TenantDb.

title: Boot seeding re-creates soft-deleted reference rows
detail: The seed lookup only considers live system-tenant rows, so a soft-deleted reference row is created anew instead of aborting the boot with a not-found error.

title: Version conflict on update reports the appended-against version
detail: The racing update path now reports expectedVersion as the stream version it appended against, also with skipOptimisticLock or an expect precondition. A failed advisory unlock after a dropped session no longer hides the migration error.

title: Unknown keys in a handler field references meta fail the boot
detail: A references meta such as `{ entity: "channel", bY: "key" }` is reported as invalid instead of silently reading as an id reference, so a misspelled `by` can no longer turn a business-key field into an id field.

title: r.requires rejects malformed arguments
detail: `r.requires` now throws when called with more than one argument or without a `features` string array, instead of dropping extra arguments or registering the object as a dependency name.

title: r.bootCheck failures keep the check's own message
detail: The boot error no longer appends a generic sentence, so messages ending in a period are not doubled and the check's text is the whole explanation.

title: Embedded list minimum stays in the JSON schema
detail: A required or `minItems` embedded list again reports `minItems` in `z.toJSONSchema` output, so agent manifests tell callers that at least one row is needed.

title: Failing trial gate no longer breaks GET /api/schema
detail: The trial gates of all disabled toggleable features run in parallel; a gate that throws counts as not unlocked, hides the add-on and is logged, so the client still boots.

title: No docsUrl for app error codes without a framework page
detail: An app subclass that overrides the error code with an uncovered reason no longer links to a framework page that does not exist; the field is absent unless errorDocs covers the reason.

title: Anonymous sessions cannot bind pending uploads on save
detail: The save pipeline now applies the same anonymous-session exclusion as the pending file ref helpers, so one visitor cannot attach another visitor's pending upload to their record.

title: Failed uploads drop their upload ledger row
detail: When the fileRef create fails after the bytes were written, POST /files and createFileRefFromBytes now delete the bytes and forget the ledger row instead of leaving it for the next sweep.

title: More HTML roots are kept out of the XML content type
detail: Uploads without a declared content type whose root element is a common HTML element (form, iframe, input, table parts, media and others) are no longer labelled application/xml.

title: POST /files uses the tenant file context and a transaction-safe upload ledger
detail: The upload route records and forgets upload bytes through the resolver's ledger like every other file context, and createFileUploadLedger throws when given a connection already inside a transaction.

title: A failed runner start no longer leaves a scheduler refresh timer behind
detail: The scheduler-seen refresh timer starts only after the rest of start() succeeded, so a failed start does not keep stamping for a runner that is not running.

title: Job runs survive a failing tenant timezone config read
detail: A throwing tenant timezone config read now logs a warning and falls back to UTC for ctx.tz instead of failing a job that never uses ctx.tz.

title: Escape-hatch process dedup no longer grows without bound
detail: Entries older than the daily re-audit interval are swept, so row-level cross-tenant read targets in long-lived workers are not kept forever.

title: Handler cross-tenant reads count in the escape-hatch metric
detail: Handlers now report to the escape-hatch meter like jobs do, so every ctx.crossTenantReads call is counted while the audit event stays deduplicated per report window.

title: beforeTransaction phase and handler share one parsed payload
detail: The payload parsed for the pre-transaction phases is handed to the handler as is, so schema defaults or transforms that generate values no longer differ between the phase and the handler.

title: Cascade delete and set-null load only child ids
detail: The cascade handler selects the id column instead of full child rows before calling the executor per child.

title: Codemods stop miscompiling or skipping ambiguous sites
detail: testing-injection rewrites named re-exports of moved names and reports export-star, testing-move reports namespace destructuring and qualified type references of split names, and object-form no longer rewrites r.requires(identifier) but reports it for a manual check.

title: schema validate names the violated FeatureDefinition key
detail: A malformed FEATURES entry now reports the first key that is missing or has the wrong type instead of always pointing at the name.

title: Upgrade check names the codemod an improvement runs on apply
detail: kumiko-upgrade without --apply now prints the codemod of each improvement entry, the same way it prints the migration of breaking entries.

title: Package-merge codemod keeps one entry per target package
detail: When the merge target is already listed in dependencies, the old devDependencies entry is dropped; when the old entry is in dependencies and the target only in devDependencies, the target moves to dependencies so the runtime entry wins.

title: NotificationTemplateMeta declares senderName and replyTo
detail: The type now matches the mail template meta schema of the template resolver, which accepts senderName and replyTo.

title: Seed writes run the save lifecycle, so seeded files bind to their records
detail: runProdApp built the boot seed dispatcher without lifecycle hooks, so seed writes and seed migrations skipped file binding (entity_id stayed null, other users got 404), the pre/post save and delete hooks, the tenant check of file references and the disposal of removed file references. The seed dispatcher now reuses the lifecycle hooks of the API dispatcher, exposed as lifecycleHooks on the entrypoints and on KumikoServer. A hook that throws inside the transaction now fails the seed and the boot.

title: English source comments without issue references in bundled-features
detail: Comments in bundled-features are translated to English, and issue numbers and planning labels are removed while the reason they stood for stays. Pure paraphrases of the code are dropped. No code changes.

title: English source comments without issue references in the framework package
detail: Comments in packages/framework are translated to English, and issue numbers and planning labels are removed while the reason they stood for stays. Pure paraphrases of the code are dropped. The ZIP entry path doc now states the UTF-8 flag the writer actually sets. No code changes.

title: English source comments without issue references in the renderer
detail: Comments in the renderer are translated to English, and issue numbers and planning labels are removed while the reason they stood for stays. Pure paraphrases of the code are dropped. No code changes; the generated widget reference (agents/widgets.md) follows the translated JSDoc.

title: English source comments without issue references in the smaller packages
detail: Comments in types, server-runtime, dev-server, guards, testing, cli, create-kumiko-app and renderer-mail-html are translated to English, and issue numbers and planning labels are removed while the reason they stood for stays. Pure paraphrases of the code are dropped. No code changes; the comment-language baseline is lowered accordingly.

title: Runtime log lines go through the process logger
detail: Modules that wrote to console now use createFallbackLogger, so once setProcessLogger is wired their lines reach the configured logger with namespace and structured fields; before that they still fall back to console. createFallbackLogger gained an info method. The `[kumiko]` prefix now comes from the logger namespace, errors travel as structured fields, and the non-JSON-safe schema assertion in buildAppSchema logs the offending path instead of the whole schema. In production the boot warnings arrive as pino JSON with a `component` field (set by the process-logger child or by `context.log.child({ component })`) instead of `[kumiko:boot]` plain text. The KEK source, the seed migration and "idle pre-check recovered" lines are logged at `info`.
