An app that sets its own `extraContext.log` receives the boot and event-dispatcher warnings in that logger.

title: MIT License for all public packages
detail: Every @cosmicdrift package and create-kumiko-app are published under MIT instead of BUSL-1.1, so hosting and platform use no longer need a commercial agreement. Earlier releases keep their BUSL-1.1 terms.

title: Fewer unchecked casts, runtime checks at boundaries
detail: bridgeStub needs no casts, the db dialect types drop any (TableColumns is SchemaTable, SelectQuery is unknown). Malformed input now fails at the boundary instead of later, for example a step that returns a non-WriteResult as the pipeline result, a non-numeric Redis counter in the login rate limiter, or r.useExtension, r.referenceData, r.job, r.notification, r.metric, r.secret, r.secretNamespace, r.claimKey and r.relation called without their required argument. Snapshot.generatedAt is optional, so snapshots written without it still load. The cast baseline is rewritten so new suspect casts in a file fail the As-Casts Audit.

title: Fail-closed projection allowlist walk, cleaner fallback log lines
detail: createFallbackLogger no longer prints a trailing `undefined` when a log call carries no data. The step walker shared by the projection allowlist check and the workflow event-trigger registration now aborts with path and index when a sub-step list holds an entry that is not a step, instead of skipping it. The `unknown` overload of `runInSavepoint` hands its callback a `DbRunner`. Log lines drop doubled namespace prefixes, and the remaining errors in eager-load, the event store and the token request route travel as structured fields.

title: ctx.crossTenantReads for handlers with the crossTenantReads grant
detail: A handler whose `escapeHatch` lists `grants: ["crossTenantReads"]` (or `unsafeRaw`, which implies it) gets `ctx.crossTenantReads` with `selectMany`, `fetchOne` and `count`, unfiltered by tenant and including the events table. Every call is audited as `cross-tenant-read`; `ctx.db.unsafeRaw()` stays denied for the read-only grant, and neither a member-resolution read nor an agent tool call (`dispatchToolCall`, including handlers it reaches through nested `ctx.query`/`ctx.write`) ever receives the surface, so cross-tenant rows cannot reach an LLM context. Jobs use the same grant. The internal `runAsDirectCallEntry` (`/internal/request-context`) now also marks its scope as an agent tool call. Without the grant nothing changes.

title: requiredLocales boot option
detail: `validateBootOptions.requiredLocales` (also `VALIDATE_BOOT_OPTIONS` in kumiko/schema.ts) makes boot fail when any translation key of the mounted features lacks one of the listed locales. Locales are combined across features, so locale packages close the gaps of the features they translate. Without the option nothing changes. This replaces the locale list the i18n-keys guard read from `src/i18n-guard-locales.ts` until 0.384.0; without that file it checked `["de", "en"]`.
migration: Define the option once, e.g. `{ requiredLocales: ["de", "en"] }`, pass it as `validateBootOptions` wherever the app boots (`runProdApp`, `runDevApp`, workers) and re-export it as `VALIDATE_BOOT_OPTIONS` from `kumiko/schema.ts` so `kumiko-schema validate` checks it in CI. The check covers framework and bundled keys too; a key missing a locale fails boot with the feature and key named.

title: selectMany distinctOn for newest-row-per-key reads
detail: SelectOptions.distinctOn takes field names and emits SELECT DISTINCT ON over them, keeping the first row per key by orderBy, so newest-row-per-key reads no longer need unsafeRaw. orderBy has to start with the distinctOn fields in the same order, otherwise selectMany throws; without orderBy it defaults to them ascending. Tenant scoping applies as for every selectMany. Error classification and driver detection drop the branches for the removed Bun.SQL driver (ERR_POSTGRES_* codes, SQLSTATE in errno, millisecond timeouts), which postgres-js never produces.

title: Boot fails when a feature leaves a locale out of some of its translation keys
detail: Within one feature, every translation key must carry every locale that any key of the same feature carries. A missing locale or an empty string fails boot with one error listing all gaps. Features with a single locale across all keys are unaffected, as are locale packages. A plural object counts as present.
migration: Add the missing locale to each listed key, or move that locale out of the feature into a locale package.

title: Entity text fields must declare a personal stance
detail: FieldsMap requires the personal stance of text and longText fields by type, and boot throws for such a field without one. The name heuristic for PII-typical names stays a warning and only applies to other field types.
migration: Move raw `{ type: "text" }` and `{ type: "longText" }` entity fields to createTextField / createLongTextField with `personal` ("self", "tenant", "ref", `{ of }`, or false with a `reason`). tsc shows each place.

title: Consumer admin functions accept a transaction, notIn where operator
detail: restartConsumer, skipPoisonEvent, disableConsumer, enableConsumer and the progress readers accept a DbRunner (pool or open transaction); skipPoisonEvent uses its own transaction on a pool and a savepoint inside a handler transaction. skipPoisonEvent takes { requireStatus } and checks it under its row lock; the consumer-skip handler requires "dead". Rejected transitions throw ConsumerTransitionError with rejection "unknown-consumer" or "wrong-status". Where clauses support { notIn: [...] }. Existing callers passing a DbConnection compile unchanged.

title: GET /files/meta?ids= returns file metadata in one request
detail: Up to 100 comma-separated file ids per call (more answers 400 too_many_ids). The same tenant and access checks as /files/:id/meta apply per id; unknown, foreign and invalid ids are left out of the answer. The renderer's file thumbnails and file names batch their lookups through it, so a list of N files no longer issues N meta requests.

title: close() ends unbounded pools of abandoned long runs
detail: withoutStatementTimeout (reindexEntity, PII backfill, projection and multi-stream rebuilds, event-store index builds) runs on its own pool without statement_timeout and closes it when the run settles. A run that never settles, such as a reindex a boot rebuild gave up on via its own timeout, kept that pool connected, so DROP DATABASE in test cleanup failed with "is being accessed by other users". The connection handle's close() now ends these pools too. A rebuild that is still running when close() is called is ended after the same close timeout instead of keeping shutdown waiting.

title: Placeholder reasons are rejected at boot and at runtime
detail: An empty, whitespace-only or placeholder reason ("todo", "tbd", "fixme", "legacy", "temp", "wip", "n/a", "none", "xxx", a "todo:" / "fixme:" / "tbd:" prefix, or the migrate-cross-tenant codemod marker) now fails boot for `openToAll.reason` and `escapeHatch.reason`, and throws at call time for `ctx.systemDb.unsafeRaw(reason)`, `acknowledgeCrossTenant(reason)`, `unsafeAllTenants: { reason }` on read steps and `declareEscapeHatch({ reason })`, which is no longer a no-op. The Escape-Hatch-Declared and Open-To-All-Reason guards that checked this statically are removed.
migration: Replace every placeholder reason with the real justification (why this access is needed and on whose right). Reasons held in imported constants were never judged by the guards and surface now, at boot or on first use.

title: loadAllEventsByType and LOAD_ALL_EVENTS_ROW_LIMIT are removed
detail: loadAllEventsByType buffered every event of an aggregate type in memory and had no production caller. It is removed together with LOAD_ALL_EVENTS_ROW_LIMIT and the Loadall-Events guard.
migration: Use `await Array.fromAsync(streamAllEventsByType(db, aggregateType))`, or iterate the stream with `for await` to stay memory-bounded. The stream is ordered by event id; loadAllEventsByType ordered by (createdAt, id).

title: metricField is removed from the screen type exports
detail: metricField is removed from the engine types and ui-types exports because MetricSpec is always an object now.
migration: Replace `metricField(metric)` with `metric.field`.

title: Text field format "iban"
detail: createTextField({ format: "iban" }) validates the value server-side (spaces ignored, case-insensitive, country and check digits shape plus mod-97) and reports invalid_format with format iban, which the form maps to errors.validation.invalid_format.iban (texts in en, de, es, fr, it). The value is stored as typed.

title: Process logger, request context fields and redaction
detail: runProdApp and runWorkerApp install a pino process logger (JSON in production) that every createFallbackLogger without an explicit logger resolves lazily, with a component field. Log lines carry requestId, correlationId, tenantId, userId, feature and handler from the request context; jobs carry tenantId and userId too. Keys such as password, token, secret, apiKey, authorization, cookie, set-cookie, x-api-key, sessionToken, privateKey, credentials, otp, iban and email are redacted to [redacted] up to depth 2. New scrubLogText masks e-mail addresses, JWTs, bearer tokens and Postgres key details in server-fault, job-failure and client-error logs.

title: POST /api/client-errors collects browser error reports
detail: Anonymous endpoint with a strict body (errorId, kind, message, stack, screen, path, buildVersion), an 8 KB cap (413), 400 without echo, a per-IP limit of 10 per minute (429, in memory per process when Redis is absent) and 204 on success. The report is logged as a scrubbed warning; the query and hash of the path are cut. With a session the report carries tenantId and userId.

title: Global IP and http-route limits fail open when Redis is down
detail: Behavior change: previously a Redis error answered 503 on these two limits. The l1-global-ip and http-route limits let the request through on a Redis error instead of answering 503, count it in kumiko_rate_limit_fail_open_total{label} and log a warning at most every 30 s. The l2-auth-endpoints and login/MFA limits stay fail-closed. A Redis client that is not ready fails fast instead of waiting for the command timeout. Redis connection loss and recovery are logged once per state change.

title: globalIpRateLimit and httpRouteRateLimit option onFailClosed is now onFailOpen
detail: The option is renamed because both limits now let the request through on a Redis error; the callback receives the error and is throttled to one warning per 30 s. Both limits also accept a meter for kumiko_rate_limit_fail_open_total.
migration: rename onFailClosed to onFailOpen in globalIpRateLimit and httpRouteRateLimit options; the callback no longer implies a 503, the request continues

title: Prod and worker pools cap statements at 60 s and idle transactions at 300 s
detail: Behavior change, not an API break. runProdApp and runWorkerApp now open their Postgres pools with statement_timeout 60 s and idle_in_transaction_session_timeout 300 s (handlers that await external calls inside a transaction are not killed early, leaked transactions still end), so one runaway query or a transaction left open no longer holds a connection indefinitely. lock_timeout stays off. Opt out per limit by setting the variable to 0, or change it, with DATABASE_STATEMENT_TIMEOUT_MS, DATABASE_IDLE_IN_TRANSACTION_TIMEOUT_MS and DATABASE_LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS (for example DATABASE_STATEMENT_TIMEOUT_MS=0); createDbConnection takes statementTimeoutMs, idleInTransactionSessionTimeoutMs and lockTimeoutMs. Migrations, projection and multi-stream rebuilds, search reindex, PII backfills and the CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY helpers run without the statement cap (withoutStatementTimeout). A custom long-running statement on the app pool now needs the same helper or a higher limit.

title: Reindex and subject purge scan by keyset instead of OFFSET
detail: reindexEntity and the subject purge page with WHERE id > last ORDER BY id LIMIT n, so rows deleted or changed while the scan runs no longer make it skip later rows.

title: Writes compile only for Writable tables or capable runners
detail: The negative ExecutorOnly brand is replaced by positive brands. table(), defineUnmanagedTable and deriveEntityTableMeta with source "unmanaged" return Writable tables; buildEntityTable and r.projection tables do not. insertOne, updateMany, deleteMany, the upsert and counter helpers and the TenantDb and db.global() write methods accept a Writable table, or any table when the runner is an ExecutorManagedRunner or ExecutorManagedTenantDb. Widening a table to SchemaTable or EntityTableMeta drops the brand, so erased tables no longer compile. Projection apply functions receive tx as ExecutorManagedRunner. The runtime lock is unchanged.
migration: Apply functions that annotate `tx` as `DbRunner`, inline or standalone, type it as `ExecutorManagedRunner` (or drop the annotation / annotate the function with SingleStreamApplyFn/MultiStreamApplyFn). Own write helpers take `WritableTable` for direct-write tables, or `ExecutorManagedRunner` / `ExecutorManagedTenantDb` when they write event-fed tables from an apply, rebuild or tenant-destroy context, instead of `SchemaTable`/`EntityTableMeta`. Tables annotated as `SchemaTable` lose the `Writable` brand; drop the annotation or add `& Writable`. Tenant-destroy hooks keep using the db they receive. Affects kumiko-enterprise, solon, money-horse, kumiko-studio, publicstatus.

title: PII backfill encrypts jsonb object and array fields
detail: runPiiEventBackfill and backfillEventPiiEncryption now retro-encrypt plaintext jsonb objects and arrays of personal fields and personal jsonb scalars, and createPiiBackfillStateTable bootstraps under an advisory lock so concurrent first boots no longer skip the ALTER. Completed backfill states rerun once because the transform version changed.

title: applyEntityEvent is exported from the db barrel, extension sources accept auto-verbs
detail: applyEntityEvent can be used by extendEntityProjection apply handlers to project stored entity events of a foreign aggregate type. validateProjectionApplyKeys accepts the entity auto-verbs for an extension source that is not a registered entity.

title: SSE entity signals follow the read access of the connection
detail: A signed-in connection receives an entity signal only when a query reading that entity lets one of its roles in (SseRouteOptions.entityReadAccess, built by collectEntityReadAccess). Entities without a reading query no longer go on the channel. When the reading access depends on a row or owner filter, the signal goes out without id and version, so a client refetches its query instead of learning which row changed.
migration: Apps that rely on a signal for an entity no query exposes to the user must add a query for that entity with a matching access rule. Custom buildServer callers that build SseRouteOptions themselves must pass entityReadAccess.

title: Cause details only with NODE_ENV development or test
detail: internal_error responses and write error infos carry the cause snapshot (name, message, stack) only when NODE_ENV is explicitly development or test. A missing or misspelled NODE_ENV no longer exposes stack traces, paths or upstream URLs. kumiko-dev starts the server with NODE_ENV=development when none is set, so local dev keeps the details; a dev script that runs the server directly (bun --watch bin/server.ts) must set NODE_ENV=development itself to see them.

title: Global IP rate-limit middleware default matches runProdApp
detail: globalIpRateLimit defaults to 600 requests per 60 seconds (was 1000). DEFAULT_GLOBAL_RATE_LIMIT is exported from the api barrel and shared with server-runtime. authEndpointRateLimit keeps its default of 5 per 60 seconds.
migration: Apps that use globalIpRateLimit directly and relied on 1000 pass limit explicitly. runProdApp users see no change.

title: Boot warning when /metrics is off in production
detail: buildServer logs a warning in production when no metrics option is set, which happens when PROMETHEUS_METRICS_TOKEN is unset.

title: Package ships its event-store table catalog
detail: kumiko-es-tables.json is included in the published files; no runtime change.

title: Direct writes on event-fed tables throw at runtime
detail: buildEntityTable and r.projection mark their tables. insertOne, updateMany, deleteMany, the upsert and counter helpers, ctx.db write methods and db.global() writes throw AccessDeniedError on a marked table unless the runner carries the framework write capability. The executor, projection apply, rebuild, unsafeProjectionDelete, tenant-destroy hooks and deleteRowsWithoutReplayableStream hold it; ctx.db.unsafeRaw() never does. Retention deletes only rows whose stream is gone or archived. The cascade delete hook, the soft-delete purge jobs and seedReferenceData now write through the executor, so their effect survives a rebuild; cascade children are written as the system user, and softDelete children are soft-deleted instead of hard-deleted. The direct-entity-writes guard has no exceptions left.
migration: Write event-fed rows through the executor (r.crud, ctx.write, createEventStoreExecutor). Projection apply functions must use the db they receive. Test seeds and teardown use seedRow, seedRows, updateRows, deleteRows and clearTables from kumiko-testing instead of hand-written wipe helpers. Do not pass ctx.db.unsafeRaw() to code that deletes event-fed rows; pass ctx.db inside a tenant-destroy hook. Retention code calls deleteRowsWithoutReplayableStream after pruning or archiving the events. seedReferenceData takes the registry instead of a table map. Affects kumiko-enterprise, kumiko-studio and solon.

title: Tests pin the money units of form derivations
detail: form-derivations tests now cover realistic money values (1234,56 EUR plus 234,57 EUR, 0,10 plus 0,20) and minor-unit list cells; no behaviour change.
migration: None.

title: A slow SSE client no longer buffers without bound
detail: The SSE route tracks the writes a client has not consumed. A client whose queued frames make no progress for SSE_STALLED_CLIENT_TIMEOUT_MS (one heartbeat interval), or that queues SSE_MAX_PENDING_WRITES_PER_CLIENT frames, is aborted and unregistered; it reconnects and resyncs. A large broadcast batch does not drop a client that keeps reading, and one failing client no longer stops the broadcast to the others. SseRouteOptions.now makes the clock injectable.

title: Deprecations name their removal release
detail: The three @deprecated APIs without a target release (the minor-units money accessor and the landingPath props of the invite and signup screens) now say they are removed in 0.390.0.

title: buildEntityTableMeta and observabilityOptions removed
detail: buildEntityTableMeta was a deprecated alias of deriveEntityTableMeta. The deprecated observabilityOptions option of the entrypoint and the prod and worker runners is gone as well, it had no effect since the HTTP route label no longer carries a query string.
migration: Rename buildEntityTableMeta to deriveEntityTableMeta (same signature). Delete observabilityOptions from the entrypoint and runner options, nothing replaces it.

title: readDatabaseNow(db) in framework/db
detail: Typed read of the Postgres clock for a TenantDb without unsafeRaw. Inside a transaction now() is the transaction start, so repeated reads agree.

title: SaveContext.event no longer reaches JSON responses
detail: The event echoed on the SaveContext of create, update and restore is non-enumerable, so a handler returning the save result no longer leaks event data (PII) in its response; hooks and projections still read it by property.

title: Dashboard navigate params may bind a record
detail: The boot validator accepts navigate params on a dashboard row action that has a record binding (record.param) but no filter; it still rejects params when the dashboard reads no filter, time range or record binding.

title: Re-export shim packages removed
detail: The shims headless, dispatcher-live, renderer-web, http and repo-manifest are gone. Their code lives in kumiko-renderer (/headless, /live, /web), kumiko-framework (/http) and kumiko-guards (/repo-manifest).
migration: Run bun kumiko-upgrade --apply, or bun kumiko codemod package-merge . --write. It rewrites the imports and package.json dependencies of all five shims to their target packages.

title: TenantDb.databaseNow
detail: TenantDb has a databaseNow() method returning Postgres now(); custom TenantDb implementations must add it.
migration: Add databaseNow(): Promise<Date> to hand-built TenantDb objects and mocks, returning the Postgres now().

title: actionForm can derive head totals from an embedded list
detail: An actionForm screen declares `derive` for head fields: sum, subtract, multiply, percent over other fields, or listSum over one cell of an embedded list with an optional whenEmpty fallback. The renderer recomputes them live and shows them read-only; a listSum without whenEmpty becomes an input while the list is empty. withFormDerivations(schema, screen) recomputes them on the server before validation, so client totals are never trusted; boot fails when the handler schema is not wrapped with the screen's own derive. A field that only feeds a `whenEmpty` fallback is read-only while the lists have rows. New embedded derived op `percent` (from[0] * from[1] / 100).
migration: Add `derive` to the actionForm screen and wrap the handler schema with `withFormDerivations(schema, screen)`; new embedded derived op `percent`.

title: Extension-selector settings form is one standard configEdit screen
detail: Without owner panels the provider form is the `<owner>-tenant` screen itself (no dashboard, no `<owner>-tenant-selection`). The provider select offers an empty "platform default" option next to the plugin ids.

title: Search index setup helpers
detail: collectSearchableFieldNames(registry) returns the deduplicated searchable fields of all entities and configureTenantSearchIndex(adapter, registry, tenantId) configures a tenant index with them, both exported from the search entry.

title: TenantDb.advisoryXactLock
detail: ctx.db.advisoryXactLock(namespace, key) takes a transaction-scoped pg_advisory_xact_lock keyed on the handle's own tenantId plus key, so tenants never contend and the caller cannot pick another tenant. It needs no unsafeRaw grant.

title: Boot check for projectionList writeHandler actions
detail: Boot now rejects projectionList rowActions and toolbarActions of kind writeHandler whose handler is not a registered write-handler QN. Such actions only failed on click before.
migration: Fix the handler QN to "<feature>:write:<short>" of a handler declared via r.writeHandler(...), or remove the action. Apps that fail to boot name the screen and action id in the error.

title: design decisions log
detail: docs/reference/decisions.md records lasting design decisions with their reasons. It is documentation only and changes no behavior.

title: Env hint links to the infra deploy runbook
detail: The boot env report ends with a link to docs/runbooks/standard-deploy-app.md in the infra repo instead of a path in kumiko-platform that no longer exists.

title: Replay parser and migration splitter cover dollar quotes, RENAME, CREATE TABLE AS and DO
detail: splitSqlStatements keeps dollar-quoted bodies whole and throws on an unterminated one. The replay parser follows RENAME TO, RENAME COLUMN, CREATE TABLE AS and DO blocks; tables with columns it cannot derive are skipped in the schema diff. The Bun.SQL wording in db/query.ts errors and logger names now says postgres-js.

title: providerPluginContextFromHandler and providerPluginContextFromJob
detail: Build a ProviderPluginContext from a HandlerContext or JobContext (jobs use the system user and have no dbOutsideTransaction).

title: hasOutsideTransactionDb and requireOutsideTransactionDb
detail: Public helpers in the db barrel. hasOutsideTransactionDb(ctx) narrows ctx.dbOutsideTransaction to TenantDb; requireOutsideTransactionDb(ctx) returns it or throws an InternalError.

title: Provider contexts expose auditUserId instead of _userId
detail: FileProviderContext, MailTransportContext, InboundMailContext and the context read by requireSecretsContext name the audit identity auditUserId. The old underscore field is gone.
migration: Rename _userId to auditUserId wherever a provider context is built by hand (tests, custom resolvers, worker wiring). requireSecretsContext still falls back to ctx.user.id when it is unset.

title: Boot always sets configAccessorFactory and overrides an app value
detail: addConfigAccessorFactory writes configAccessorFactory and the _configAccessorFactory alias from the effective configResolver, replacing any app-supplied factory. The replay parser also rejects DO blocks without a dollar-quoted body and accepts tags like $do1$.

title: http moved into framework
detail: egress(), the host policy helpers and their errors are implemented in @cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/http. @cosmicdrift/kumiko-http now only re-exports that subpath and is removed after the consumer pass of wave 4.
migration: Run bun kumiko-upgrade --apply, or bun kumiko codemod package-merge . --write. It rewrites imports of @cosmicdrift/kumiko-http to @cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/http and replaces the kumiko-http dependency in package.json with kumiko-framework.

title: package-merge codemod covers headless and dispatcher-live
detail: The mapping table of the package-merge codemod gained the headless and dispatcher-live moves into kumiko-renderer.

title: package-merge codemod covers renderer-web and CSS files
detail: The mapping table of the package-merge codemod gained the renderer-web move into kumiko-renderer/web, and the codemod now also rewrites .css files (@import, @plugin, @config). A @source path into the old package is reported for manual follow-up.

title: kumiko-upgrade writes CHANGELOG.md and shows manual entries with --verbose
detail: --apply adds one section per bump to CHANGELOG.md in the app (changed packages, breaking titles, manual migrations with status, codemods applied); a re-run of the same bump replaces its section. --verbose prints detail and migration of the open manual entries. A second --apply keeps the codemods already recorded in the marker. The biome-app preset allows console in bin and scripts. AppConfig takes an optional includeBundled flag that the managed kumiko/schema.ts uses to compose the bundled auth features.

title: actionForm successLinks and resetOnSuccess
detail: successLinks keeps the actionForm open after a successful submit and lists links resolved like redirect; boot rejects it together with redirect, with an unknown target or with a record target without idFrom. resetOnSuccess clears typed values after success. Role projection drops links to screens the role cannot reach.

title: clientAction row actions
detail: RowAction gains kind "clientAction" with a client-registered handler name; boot rejects a name that is not <feature>:<kebab>, and the surface keys include its confirm, confirmLabel and successMessage.

title: Boot validation for screen-panel fallback and text panels
detail: DashboardScreenPanel.fallback needs visibleWhen and a registered, embeddable target without its own visibleWhen. DashboardTextPanel (kind "text", exported with DashboardTextBlock) rejects empty blocks and empty lists; its text keys are required translation keys. Extension-selector panels qualify a short fallback ref, and role projection drops a fallback the role cannot reach.

title: Dashboard record binding, header actions, refresh and relative time
detail: Dashboards take record, actions and refresh; stat panels and text params gain a relativeTime format; the surface keys include kumiko.dashboard.record.missing.

title: DashboardChartPanel.valueFormat only takes the currency format
detail: DashboardValueFormat is now a union of DashboardCurrencyFormat and DashboardRelativeTimeFormat. Stat panels take both, chart panels only the currency one, and boot rejects relativeTime on a chart.
migration: A chart panel that declares valueFormat keeps working with { kind: "currency", currency }. Code that types a chart's valueFormat as DashboardValueFormat should use DashboardCurrencyFormat instead; relativeTime on a chart was never meaningful and now fails boot.

title: Derived list searchability, actionForm load and drawer rowClick
detail: projectionList searchable is derived false for entity-convention lists without searchable fields (searchable true is rejected at boot), actionForm.load registers a query checked at boot, and a drawer row action may set rowClick, counted with navigate rowClick and rejected on projectionDetail header actions.

title: Boot checks for field affixes and fillAction
detail: Boot fails when a fillAction query is not a registered query handler, or when a { field } affix or a fillAction params source is not a field of the same form.

title: pagedListSchema and pageRows for in-memory list queries
detail: pagedListSchema(sortableFields) and pageRows(rows, request, { searchFields, defaultSort }) cover search, sort (missing values last, ties by id), offset paging and an optional total for projectionList queries over merged rows. PagedListRequest and PagedListRowValue are exported; nextCursor is always null.

title: DashboardProgressTone type and unlimited label key
detail: New exported type DashboardProgressTone for progress-list row tones. The default translations gain kumiko.dashboard.progress.unlimited.

title: Dashboard chart panels take a y-axis unit
detail: DashboardChartPanel.unit (i18n key) is shown once on the y axis of a timeseries chart, with or without valueFormat. The boot validator rejects unit on other chart kinds; an untranslated unit key fails the required-surface key check.

title: loadPendingFileRef and bindPendingFileRef bind a caller's own pending upload from a custom handler
detail: Additive. fileName is not part of PendingFileRef because it is personal data; read it via the fileRef executor's detail. Unexpected update errors throw; version_conflict and unique_violation map to "version-conflict".

title: rateLimit accepts a list of buckets that are enforced all-or-nothing
detail: RateLimitDeclaration is now a single option, a non-empty list of options or the disabled form. RateLimitResolver gains the required method enforceAll(requests: readonly RateLimitBucketRequest[]); createRateLimitResolver and createUnlimitedRateLimitResolver implement it. Payload buckets in additionalRateLimits are charged through the same call.
migration: Custom RateLimitResolver implementations and test fakes need an enforceAll method (check every bucket, then deduct from all or none, and throw RateLimitError for the rejected bucket with the largest retryAfter). Existing rateLimit declarations stay valid. A duplicate payloadField in additionalRateLimits is now a boot error; merge the entries into one.

title: kumiko check validates the boot configuration with the validateBootOptions from kumiko.config.ts
detail: Set validateBootOptions in defineAppConfig (navAllowlist, navAllowlistExempt, warnOnUniqueAccessRoles); the managed kumiko/schema.ts exports it as VALIDATE_BOOT_OPTIONS and kumiko check validates with it. Apps with a hand-written kumiko/schema.ts can export VALIDATE_BOOT_OPTIONS themselves.
migration: Existing apps get the new line in kumiko/schema.ts through `kumiko-upgrade --apply` (managed file). The bin files belong to the app: pass `...(appConfig.validateBootOptions && { validateBootOptions: appConfig.validateBootOptions })` to runProdApp in bin/main.ts and to runDevApp in bin/server.ts (import appConfig from "../kumiko.config") so runtime and kumiko check agree.

title: createEntity no longer collapses to never for inline field literals such as { type: "reference", entity }
detail: The fields type parameter is const, so the literal type of each inline field survives without as const.

title: executor.detail() and executor.list() return EntityRow<E>, derived from the entity definition
detail: Rows of createEntityExecutor / createEventStoreExecutor are typed per entity; wide entities keep Record<string, unknown>. createBooleanField is typed non-null. UserMfaRow in the bundled auth-mfa feature now declares enabledAt and lastUsedAt as Temporal.Instant, which is what the row always held.
migration: Remove the `row as T` casts on executor.detail() / executor.list() results with `bun kumiko-upgrade --apply` (codemod remove-engine-payload-casts). Casts to a type the row does not satisfy stay and are listed as manual; replace them with a field-level check or a narrower type.

title: A save cannot reference a file that belongs to another record
detail: Creating or updating a record with a file id that is already bound to a different record of the same tenant is now rejected with invalid_element on that field, the same error as for a foreign tenant. Pending uploads, ids the record already holds and moves between its own file fields are unaffected.

title: Tokens carrying system or all lose those roles on verify
detail: jwt.verify strips the system and all roles that session minting never grants, so a self-signed or leaked-key token cannot act as System.
migration: Apps that mint their own tokens with the `system` role must stop doing so and use `createSystemUser` or system dispatch in-process instead. Tokens issued by the framework are unaffected. Tests that send a system user over `stack.http.*` must switch to `stack.dispatcher.write/query`.

title: http.route and the metric route label carry the route pattern, http.target is removed
detail: Spans are named "METHOD pattern" instead of "http.request"; paths no route matched are labelled "unmatched". The PII ciphertext guard message names the pattern as well.
migration: Dashboards, alerts and trace queries keyed on raw paths or on the span name "http.request" must switch to route patterns and the "METHOD pattern" span name. Read the query string from your access logs if you relied on http.target.

title: Dry-run env table and boot check respect required overrides and the fileStorage default
detail: The env table of KUMIKO_DRY_RUN_ENV=boot shows a variable as required when the app schema overlays required() on an optional field, and the error says required. The schema-cli boot check applies runProdApp's fileStorage default instead of demanding FILE_STORAGE_PROVIDER.

title: inspectEnv, renderEnvInspection and the dry-run mode parser
detail: inspectEnv(schema, env, { sources }) checks each field on its own and returns its status (set, unset, missing, invalid) without the value; renderEnvInspection renders those rows as the boot table. parseDryRunEnvMode reads KUMIKO_DRY_RUN_ENV (1, true, human, json, pulumi, k8s, boot) and isDryRunEnvActive tells module-level code whether a dry run is running. DRY_RUN_ENV_VAR names the variable.

title: createEnvMasterKeyProvider defers the keyring check in a dry run
detail: While KUMIKO_DRY_RUN_ENV is set, createEnvMasterKeyProvider no longer throws at construction on a missing or malformed keyring; the first key operation throws instead. Apps that build the provider at module load can run the boot dry run on an empty env. Outside a dry run the check still runs at construction, and the boot probe for encrypted entity fields forces it in both cases.

title: composeEnvSchema returns a typed schema
detail: composeEnvSchema infers the merged shape from core, extend and every feature typed with featureWithEnvSchema(feature, schema), so parseEnv(composed.schema, …) returns typed values instead of a string record. optionalFeatures types those fields optional. A feature list widened to FeatureDefinition[] still compiles and contributes no keys to the type. extend may now repeat a feature's field when it is the same instance, so an app can spread a block such as stripeEnvSchema next to the mounted feature; a different field under that key still throws.

title: import-extensions codemod and tsconfig options for .ts import specifiers
detail: The import-extensions codemod rewrites relative import and export specifiers that end in .js or .jsx to the .ts or .tsx file next to the importer (import, export from, import type, import() and mock.module). It leaves a specifier alone and reports it when no such file exists. The framework repo itself now imports with .ts endings; its published dist is unchanged. tsc writes .js into the dist, and the .d.ts files keep .ts specifiers, which TypeScript resolves to the sibling .d.ts. An app tsconfig needs allowImportingTsExtensions: true, because the framework packages now ship sources with .ts specifiers and tsc checks them (the preset @cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/tsconfig.app.json sets it). A tsconfig that emits JS also needs rewriteRelativeImportExtensions (TypeScript 5.7 or newer); a project that only type-checks code from another project reference needs rewriteRelativeImportExtensions false plus emitDeclarationOnly. Consumer code with .js endings keeps running once the option is set.
migration: Add `allowImportingTsExtensions: true` to the app tsconfig (or extend @cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/tsconfig.app.json), then run the codemod (bun node_modules/@cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/src/scripts/codemod/import-extensions.ts . --write); the guard import-extensions reports remaining .js specifiers.

title: defineAppConfig in @cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/config, plus biome and tsconfig presets for apps
detail: kumiko.config.ts default-exports defineAppConfig({ features, prodFeatures?, client: { entries }, ports: { dev, e2e, infra? } }). defineAppConfig throws on ports outside 1..65535, a port claimed twice within the app, an empty client.entries list and entries that leave the app. allAppFeatures(config) returns features plus prodFeatures. New exports @cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/biome (Biome 2.5.7 preset with vcs.useIgnoreFile false) and @cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/tsconfig.app.json; an app's biome.json and tsconfig.json extend them and keep their own overrides next to extends.

title: createDbConnection takes only the options object, the bun-db subpath is gone
detail: The positional createDbConnection(url, options) overload and the deprecated @cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/bun-db subpath are removed. createDbConnection({ url, ...options }) and the query helpers come from @cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/db. Removed from /bun-db: DeleteManyBatchedOptions, DeleteManyBatchedResult, IncrementCounterOptions, InnerJoinRow, InnerJoinSpec, InsertOnConflictDoNothingOptions, JoinColumnPair, JsonTextMatch, SelectOptions, TableInfo, UpsertOnConflictOptions, WhereObject, WhereOperator, WhereValue, aggregateWhere, asEntityTableMeta, asRawClient, countWhere, deleteMany, deleteManyBatched, extractTableInfo, fetchOne, incrementCounter, insertMany, insertOnConflictDoNothing, insertOne, instantToTimestamptzParam, isTimestamptzType, requireEntityTableMeta, runInSavepoint, runInSavepointIfSupported, runnerCanBeginTransaction, selectInnerJoin, selectMany, transaction, unsafeReadRetrying, updateMany, upsertByPk, upsertOnConflict.
migration: Run bun kumiko-upgrade --apply. It rewrites positional calls to createDbConnection({ url, ... }) and moves bun-db imports to @cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/db.

title: DB_PROVIDER other than postgres fails at boot
detail: dbConnectionOptionsFromEnv used to ignore DB_PROVIDER, so DB_PROVIDER=bun booted postgres-js while the deployment still claimed Bun.SQL. Any value other than empty or "postgres" now throws with a hint to remove the variable.
migration: Remove DB_PROVIDER from the environment, Helm values and Pulumi config. postgres-js is the only driver.

title: createTenantDb takes only the options object
detail: The positional createTenantDb(db, tenantId, ...) overload is removed. createTenantDb({ db, tenantId, ... }) is the only form.
migration: Run bun kumiko-upgrade --apply. It rewrites positional calls to createTenantDb({ db, tenantId, ... }).

title: The test stack is no longer re-exported from the framework
detail: The subpaths @cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/stack, /testing, /testing/handler-context, /testing/real-providers and /testing/e2e-generator are removed, and so is the optional peer dependency on @cosmicdrift/kumiko-testing. The test stack and helpers live only in @cosmicdrift/kumiko-testing. Removed from /stack: CreateTestDbOptions, EventCollector, RequestHelper, TestDb, TestRedis, TestStack, TestStackOptions, TestUsers, createEventCollector, createRequestHelper, createTestDb, createTestRedis, createTestUser, drainEventConsumers, pushEntityProjectionTables, resetEventStore, setupTestStack, testTenantId, testUserId, unsafeCreateEntityTable, unsafeEnsureEntityTable, unsafePushTables. Removed from /testing and its subpaths: ClearableTable, E2EGeneratorOptions, E2ETestSpec, EditFillOp, LateBoundHolder, ManualClock, MutableMasterKeyProvider, ParsedSetCookie, REAL_PROVIDERS_ENV, RecordingProvider, bridgeStub, buildMultipartBody, captureClosedConnectionError, clearTables, createLateBoundHolder, createManualClock, createMutableMasterKeyProvider, createRecordingProvider, createTestEnvelopeCipher, createTestMasterKeyProvider, deleteRows, describeFileProviderContract, expectError, expectErrorIncludes, expectSuccess, generateE2ESpec, generateZodFixture, getSetCookieRaw, getSetCookieValue, getSetCookies, isRealProviderRun, patchFileInstanceofForBunTest, requireRealProviders, resetBlindIndexKeyForTests, resetEntityFieldEncryptionCacheForTests, resetEventPiiCatalogForTests, resetPiiSubjectKmsForTests, resetTestTables, rolesOf, seedRow, seedRows, sharedItemEntity, sharedItemTable, sharedUserEntity, sharedUserTable, sharedWidgetEntity, sharedWidgetTable, sleep, updateRows, waitFor, withBootValidatorFixture, withoutAmbientTemporal, zipWithEntries.
migration: Run bun kumiko-upgrade --apply. It moves the imports to the matching @cosmicdrift/kumiko-testing subpaths. Add @cosmicdrift/kumiko-testing to devDependencies if it is not there yet.

title: createEventDef builds an EventDef without a registrar
detail: createEventDef({ feature, name, schema, version?, piiFields? }) from @cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/engine returns the same EventDef that r.defineEvent returns, including the PII field validation, so shared event definitions can live outside a defineFeature callback.

title: escapeHatch on a spread entity query handler requires SystemAdmin access
detail: A query handler that spreads defineEntityListHandler or defineEntityDetailHandler and adds escapeHatch afterwards skipped the SystemAdmin-only access check that the factory option enforces. Registration now applies the same check and throws for any other access.
migration: Pass escapeHatch as an option of defineEntityListHandler or defineEntityDetailHandler with access { roles: access.systemAdmin }, or write a plain r.queryHandler that does not reuse the entity convention handler when a tenant-scoped query needs a raw lookup.

title: kumiko-upgrade --apply runs codemods of improvement entries too
detail: The apply step only ran codemods attached to breaking entries. The 0.368.0 entry that moves the test stack to kumiko-testing is an improvement with a codemod (testing-move), so `bun kumiko-upgrade --apply` skipped it and left the deprecated framework paths in place. Every pending entry with a codemod now runs, in version order; manual-migration reporting is unchanged. Apps whose marker is already at 0.368.0 no longer see that entry as pending, so they run `bun kumiko-upgrade --apply --from 0.367.0` once, or the codemod directly: `bun node_modules/@cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/src/scripts/codemod/testing-move.ts . --write`.

title: Append version conflicts carry currentVersion and no longer poison the transaction
detail:
append() inserts with ON CONFLICT (tenant_id, aggregate_id, version) DO NOTHING and reads the stream version in the still-intact transaction. VersionConflictError gets an optional currentVersion, and custom writes (ctx.appendEvent, stream.append, appendEventInTenantDb) now answer 409 with the winner's version instead of -1, so a client can rebase. A missing predecessor reports the real stream version too.

Behaviour change: a lost append race no longer raises a unique violation, so the outer transaction is not aborted (25P02). A handler that catches the VersionConflictError keeps writing and commits. Idempotency-key collisions still throw IdempotentAppendConflictError. Relies on READ COMMITTED, the Postgres default.

title: createDbConnection({ url, ... }) is the only connection factory, query helpers move from /bun-db to /db
detail:
postgres-js is the only DB driver. createDbConnection takes one options object, is synchronous and accepts the new options ssl and onNotice. The Bun.SQL provider, createConnection, createPgConnection and DB_PROVIDER are removed. The query helpers (selectMany, insertOne, transaction, asRawClient, ...) keep their API and are now exported from @cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/db. The `tx` handed to the transaction() callback is typed as DbTx (the postgres-js transaction handle it always was at runtime) instead of the Bun.SQL instance type; a helper that takes `db: DbConnection` and receives that tx needs `DbRunner` or `DbTx`.

The positional form createDbConnection(url, options) and the @cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/bun-db subpath keep working as deprecated aliases and are removed in the first release after 2026-10-29.

old -> new:
  createConnection(url, options) (async) -> createDbConnection({ url, ...options }) (sync)
  createPgConnection(url, options) -> createDbConnection({ url, ...options })
  createDbConnection(url, options) -> createDbConnection({ url, ...options }) (positional form is deprecated)
  @cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/bun-db -> @cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/db (deprecated alias until the first release after 2026-10-29)

Removed without replacement: createBunDbConnection, bunDbConnectionOptionsFromEnv, the BunDbConnection, BunDbTx, BunDbRunner and BunDbConnectionOptions types, DbPoolHandle (use DbConnectionHandle), the PgListenClient re-export from /bun-db (import it from @cosmicdrift/kumiko-types/db-connection) and the DB_PROVIDER environment variable.
migration: Run `bun kumiko-upgrade --apply`. It rewrites bun-db imports to /db, createDbConnection(url, options) and createConnection/createPgConnection calls to the object form, and reports leftovers (removed Bun.SQL exports, DB_PROVIDER) with file and line. Remove DB_PROVIDER from your env files.

title: Bundled feature constants become create*Feature() factories
detail:
Every bundled feature that was mounted as a constant (tagsFeature, ledgerFeature, authFoundationFeature, ...) now has a create<Name>Feature() factory exported from the same subpath, and apps mount `createTagsFeature()` instead of `tagsFeature`. Factories of features without options take no arguments; the ones that already had options keep them. Two calls of a factory give interchangeable instances, so mounting the same feature from two stacks does not trip the "mounted twice as distinct instances" check.

The old constants keep working as deprecated aliases and are removed in the first release after 2026-10-29.

old -> new:
  tagsFeature -> createTagsFeature()
  ledgerFeature -> createLedgerFeature()
  authFoundationFeature -> createAuthFoundationFeature()
  fooBarFeature -> createFooBarFeature() (same rule for every bundled feature constant)
  typeof tagsFeature -> ReturnType<typeof createTagsFeature>
migration: Run `bun kumiko-upgrade --apply`. It renames the imports and replaces every use with the factory call. It reports aliased imports, re-exports, namespace access, dynamic imports and files that compare a feature by identity with file and line; handle those by hand (one factory call per mount, or keep one shared instance).

title: List filters can no longer probe secret, encrypted or personal fields
detail:
A `filter`/`filters` entry on a field with `find: "secret"`, `encrypted: true` or a personal-data annotation made hit count and `totalCount` a value oracle (a prefix oracle for legacy plaintext rows before the backfill). The list handler now answers 400 `validation_error` with a field issue `field_not_filterable` (path `filter.<field>`). The one exception is `op: "eq"` with a string on a personal field with `find: "exact"` or `"fuzzy"`, which matches through the blind index. A sort on such a field falls back to id order instead of failing. Unknown fields are still dropped and fields without read access still match nothing; both checks run first.

The entityList boot validator rejects a screen `filter` the handler would reject.

Behaviour change: clients that filter on such a field (or send `in`, range or `ne` on a blind-indexed one) now get a 4xx instead of an empty or matching result.

title: whenAbsent "self" keys ownerless personal fields on the record instead of the tenant
detail:
A personal field with a nullable owner can now declare `personal: { of: "ownerId", whenAbsent: "self" }` (entity fields and `defineEvent` piiFields). While the owner is empty, the value is encrypted under `record:<entity>:<id>`, the same subject as `personal: "self"` on events and `personal: { of: "id" }` on entities. `forget-subject` on that record then erases the value, its blind index and its search document; with `"tenant"` the value stayed readable until the tenant was destroyed. A row can mix subjects: the ciphertext names its key inline, so owner-keyed, tenant-keyed and record-keyed fields decrypt side by side.

The boot validator accepts "self" next to "tenant" and rejects it on `idType: "serial"` entities, because a forget-subject request needs a UUID record id. Owner transitions behave as for "tenant": when an update assigns an owner (absent to X) the value moves from the record key to the user key; the created event stays record-keyed. The data-retention hardDelete also erases the record key of an ownerless "self" row; a row with an owner keeps its owner key.
migration:
Switching an existing field from `whenAbsent: "tenant"` to `"self"` changes only new writes. Events and rows written earlier stay tenant-keyed (still readable) until the PII event backfill re-keys them. The backfill fingerprint is bumped (`owner-rekey-v2`), so the boot-time backfill runs one more full pass: tenant-keyed values of rows without an owner move under their record key, tenant-keyed values of rows with an owner still move under that owner. The pass rewrites event payloads in place through the existing backfill path and queues the affected projections for rebuild. Apps that run the backfill manually call `backfillEventPiiEncryption` with `resolveOwnerFromProjection: true, rekeyTenantKeyedOwnerFields: true`, then rebuild the projections. Values of a record forgotten earlier become `[[erased]]`. The re-key covers entity lifecycle events only: custom `defineEvent` piiFields that switch from `whenAbsent: "tenant"` to `"self"` keep their old events tenant-keyed.

Old events are never reinterpreted at read time: an old created event of a row that got an owner later keeps its record key until a forget of that record, which erases it, while the later owner-keyed copies stay readable.

title: createTenantDb({ db, tenantId, ... }) takes one options object
detail:
createTenantDb takes one CreateTenantDbOptions object ({ db, tenantId, mode?, tracer?, meter?, signal?, grants? }); mode still defaults to "tenant". The positional form createTenantDb(db, tenantId, mode, tracer, meter, signal, grants) keeps working as a deprecated overload and is removed in the first release after 2026-10-29.

old -> new:
  createTenantDb(db, tenantId) -> createTenantDb({ db, tenantId })
  createTenantDb(db, tenantId, "system", tracer, meter, signal, grants) -> createTenantDb({ db, tenantId, mode: "system", tracer, meter, signal, grants })
migration: Run `bun kumiko-upgrade --apply`. It rewrites positional calls (literal undefined arguments are dropped) and reports spread arguments, calls with more than seven arguments and uses of createTenantDb as a value (callback, .bind/.call/.apply) with file and line.

title: HandlerContext and AppContext no longer expose _userId and _handlerType
detail: The dispatcher no longer sets _userId and _handlerType on the context of write handlers, query handlers and hooks. The caller identity is ctx.user.id in handlers and result.event.createdBy in postSave and postDelete hooks. requireSecretsContext reads ctx._userId first and falls back to ctx.user.id, so passing a handler context to it keeps the same audit identity. Provider contexts (FileProviderContext, MailTransportContext, InboundMailContext) keep their own _userId. JobContext._userId is unchanged.
migration: Replace ctx._userId with ctx.user.id in write and query handlers. postSave and postDelete hooks get an AppContext without user; read the caller there from result.event.createdBy. Known sites: one file each in money-horse, offlot-app, phronexsis and kumiko-enterprise. _handlerType had no readers.

title: Test stack and helpers moved to kumiko-testing, old framework paths are deprecated
migration: Run `bun kumiko-upgrade --apply`. It rewrites imports from the old paths and splits mixed imports by target. Add @cosmicdrift/kumiko-testing to devDependencies where it is missing.

title: Seed context finds template resources again
detail: findTemplateResources in the seed context filtered on an is_deleted column that the template resource table does not have, so every seed that read template resources failed. The query now reads the live rows only.

title: Seeds can store files and see why a write failed
detail: ProdSeedFn deps now carry createFileRef(tenantId, input), which stores bytes as a fileRef with the same validation and storage layout as POST /files, without a helper write handler. A seed write that fails with internal_error now names the handler and the cause message instead of a bare "internal error". The seed dispatcher gets the app's dispatcherOptions (and the job runner in all-in-one mode), like the HTTP dispatcher. The "ctx.files is unavailable" message of createFileRefFromBytes names the real cause: the dispatcher context has no file-provider resolver.

title: One injectable Clock for ctx.tz in handlers and jobs
detail: New type Clock and TzContextOptions.clock. AppContext.clock feeds ctx.tz.now() in handlers, and JobContext.tz gives jobs the same ctx.tz API (tenant timezone from tenant config, read once per job run, UTC fallback). The testing helper createManualClock(start) returns a clock with set and advance. The tenant-lifecycle job now reads time through ctx.tz.now().
migration: Code that builds a JobContext literal itself (boot seeds, test doubles) adds `tz: createTzContext()`.

title: Handler input references work on nested fields and record keys
detail: The references meta on handler input schemas is now found on fields inside arrays, nested objects and records, and on record keys. The new readHandlerFieldReferences and handlerFieldReferences return each hit with a path such as "channels[].channelKey" or "labels{key}" plus typed path segments. Boot validation checks nested references too and names the path in its error message. readHandlerFieldReference and handlerFieldReference behave as before.

title: Registrar methods take a single object, positional calls throw at registration
migration: Run `bun kumiko-upgrade --apply`. It rewrites every positional r.writeHandler, r.queryHandler, r.entity, r.requires, r.hook and registerEntityCrud call to the object form. Calls it cannot resolve statically (a spread argument, a registrar that is not typed as FeatureRegistrar) are listed as manual work with file and line; rewrite those by hand.

title: The app schema no longer lists screens, navs and workspaces of features a tenant has switched off
detail: A feature declared with r.toggleable() that is off for the caller's tenant (tier engine or feature toggles) used to stay in the nav while all its handlers answered 403 feature_disabled. GET /api/schema now drops its screens, navs, content collections and workspaces for that tenant, and every action, redirect, nav parent and workspace member that pointed at them is removed too. Entities and translations stay. The response is cached per role set and per set of disabled features, so tenants with the same set share one ETag. Without an effectiveFeatures resolver nothing changes.

title: selectMany supports column projection via SelectOptions.fields
detail: SelectOptions gains fields, a list of entity field names. selectMany then selects only those columns instead of all of them. An empty list or a name that is not a column of the table throws.

title: kumiko-upgrade names each pending manual step by an id
detail: Every pending manual step of kumiko-upgrade now has a stable id, derived from the release version and the step title. The text output shows it in brackets and the JSON output carries it as manualId, so a script or an agent can tell steps apart and record which ones it has done.

title: App and worker boot wait for Postgres instead of crashing
detail: runProdApp and worker processes now probe the database before the schema-drift check and retry with exponential backoff (1s to 15s, up to 90s) on transient connection errors such as too_many_connections or ECONNREFUSED. The KMS health check at boot retries the same way. Non-transient errors like auth failures still abort immediately.

title: Restoring a soft-deleted row with a money field no longer fails with a 500
detail: restore() wrote the raw stored row (money as bigint minor units) into payload.previous, and the jsonb bind threw. It now builds previous in the same domain form as delete(), so the restored event carries { amount, currency, ... } for money fields.

title: version_conflict from delete, restore, forget and update reports the actual stream version
detail: After a lost append race, delete, restore and forget returned currentVersion -1 and update returned the version read before the race, so expectedVersion and currentVersion looked equal. They now look up the stream version after the conflict; -1 remains only when that lookup fails.

title: ctx.forTenant is available read-only in the beforeTransaction phase
detail: A beforeTransaction phase can now resolve ctx.forTenant(tenantId) for its own tenant and, as a SystemAdmin, for a foreign tenant, to read rows or build tenant-scoped inputs such as uploads. The returned db denies every write; a foreign tenant stays gated by the SystemAdmin check. reserveBeforeTransaction, perCommand and in-transaction handlers are unchanged.

title: Boot checks from the review round 1 release reject configurations that used to boot
detail:
These checks shipped as fixes without migration notes. Each one throws for a configuration that was accepted before:
- a where-rule subquery on a table whose columns cannot be derived
- a drawer prefill that targets a sensitive field or a field the form does not render
- two secret fields with the same id
- access.personalData "public-intake" combined with rateLimit: { disabled: true }
- a recordOwned field on an entity with idType "serial"
- dedupeFeatures for same-named features with different registrations
The agent-tools manifest check in buildToolCatalog throws when the catalog is built for a request, not at boot.
migration: Boot every app against the new version before rolling it out, and send one agent tool request if the app mounts agent-tools. Give where-rule subqueries a table with derivable columns, prefill only rendered non-sensitive fields, make secret field ids unique, give public-intake handlers a rateLimit that is not disabled, switch recordOwned entities to idType "uuid" or change the field's personal stance, and rename or align duplicated features.

title: Boot rejects visibleWhen queries with required input, non-sql index where clauses, lockedWhen on read-restricted fields and same-named features with a different surface
detail:
These checks used to be absent or silent and now stop the app at boot:
- A screen or dashboard panel visibleWhen that names a query whose input schema does not accept an empty payload. The client gate runs it with an empty payload, so the screen stayed hidden.
- An entity index where that is not a sql expression. It used to be dropped, which built a full (unique) index.
- A lockedWhen field that declares access.read.
- Two features with the same name whose screens, navs, jobs, events, translations, config keys, notifications, metrics or hooks differ. The second one used to be dropped.
migration: Boot each app once against the new version. For a visibleWhen query, make its input fields optional or point visibleWhen at an input-free query. Write index where clauses with sql`...`. Remove access.read from the lockedWhen field or lock on a field every role can read. Give differing same-named features distinct names or make their surfaces identical.

title: Bun.SQL provider parity fixes for DB_PROVIDER=bun
detail: Array params bind as Postgres array literals, transaction handles are detected correctly, Instant params are stored at millisecond precision, integer params reject fractions, and migrations hold their advisory lock on one pinned connection. LISTEN/NOTIFY uses Bun.SQL listen() on its own connection, which the pool idle timeout does not close, so the Bun provider no longer opens a postgres-js peer.

title: cardColumnRoles skips hideOnNarrow images
detail: The first image column that is not hideOnNarrow becomes the card preview; narrow-hidden image columns neither become the preview nor the title.

title: Console-spy tests only count the messages of the code under test
detail: Unit tests that asserted a silent console.warn/error ran in a process shared with other test files and picked up unrelated async warnings. They now filter the spied calls to the messages the tested code produces. No runtime change.

title: AGENTS.md covers the gaps from the agent-docs eval; new dashboard-stats recipe
detail: AGENTS.md now explains personalData "tenant-members" for openToAll writes, personal { of: "id" } for records that are the person, counting with list filter and totalCount instead of filtering one page, the dashboard stat panels, that schema:generate needs a name and that a newly mounted bundled feature needs a migration, and that r.crud needs write.access and read.access. The new dashboard-stats recipe shows a dashboard with a stat-group and a stat backed by one counting query. No runtime change.

title: Same-named features that differ in screens, navs, jobs, events or hooks no longer merge silently
detail: dedupeFeatures now compares the keys of screens, navs, jobs, events, translations, config keys, notifications, metrics and hooks in addition to entities and handlers, so a second same-named feature with different surface throws instead of being dropped.

title: Moved file ids are not disposed
detail: disposeRemovedFileRefs now collects the file ids still stored in any file field of the saved record before soft-deleting removed ones, so an id moved from one field to another stays readable.

title: A .docx upload must contain a word/ entry, not just the bytes "word/"
detail: validateFileContent now reads the ZIP central directory and requires an entry name that starts with word/. ZIPs with entries such as password/a.txt or xl/word/sheet.xml, or the bytes appearing anywhere in the file, are rejected as content_mismatch.

title: zipWithEntries test helper in @cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/testing
detail: Builds a minimal ZIP with a real central directory for upload tests. Hand-made docx fixtures that only had a local header and the word/ bytes no longer pass the content check; build them with zipWithEntries("word/document.xml") instead.

title: Executor update and delete with writePurpose erasure, and forget, write the erased sentinel for subjects whose key is gone
detail: Re-encrypting a pre-KMS plaintext row after eraseKey threw subject-erased, so the erase flows could not finish their own follow-up writes. Update and delete with writePurpose erasure, and forget always, now replace the PII fields of an erased subject in changes and previous with the sentinel; fields of other subjects in the same row stay encrypted. Without writePurpose and for restore the subject-erased conflict stays. The forget-subject door close and the forget cleanup pass writePurpose erasure to the user lifecycle update.

title: Error docsUrl falls back to the framework page of the error code for uncovered app reasons
detail: An error whose details.reason is an app reason not covered by errorDocs, such as the not_found reason of every NotFoundError, now carries docsUrl pointing at the framework page of its error code (for example /errors/not_found) instead of no docsUrl. Reasons covered by errorDocs keep the app link; framework reasons are unchanged.

title: Escape-hatch audits are collected for the whole stream
detail: Dispatched streams run inside the escape-hatch audit scope for the full lifetime of the stream, and settled pending audits are dropped from the scope, so writes made while a stream is open are no longer missed.

title: Soft-delete cleanup and hardDelete retention delete the bytes of handed-over files
detail: A tenant handover moves a fileRef row to the new tenant, but its storageKey keeps the previous tenant's prefix. The soft-delete cleanup and the data-retention hardDelete went through `ctx.files.ref()` and `ctx.files.list()`, which reject keys outside the job's tenant, so the bytes and derivatives of such files were never deleted and the soft-delete cleanup kept the row forever. Both now delete through the new `deleteFileRefBytes(files, row, context)` from `@cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/derivatives`, built on the new `FileContext.listFromFileRef(row)` (the row's key plus its derivatives, under the same trust as `refFromFileRef`). Form-draft discard deletes draft files through `refFromFileRef` as well.

title: Removing a file that was moved to another file field of the same record deletes its fileRef
detail: The fileRef stayed bound to the field it was first uploaded to. Once it was moved to a second field and then removed from that field, the dispose step skipped it and the file stayed readable. Dispose now accepts a binding to any file field of the same record.

title: MFA verify without a switch-tenant gate fails at boot, and the gate result carries the session roles
detail: createAuthRoutes throws when mfaVerifyHandler is set without switchTenantMfaGateHandler, and runDevApp and runProdApp check that the gate handler is registered before wiring, so a missing gate can no longer let switch-tenant skip MFA. The gate handler returns the roles with its clear result and the route mints the target session from them. assertRetiredCookieDomains is no longer exported, and the auth-session signup variant is composed from SignupOutcome. Setups that set mfaVerifyHandler must also register the switch-tenant gate handler.

title: fetchForWriting reads one consistent stream version, nested ctx.write calls run in order, ctx.notify works through ctx.query
detail: fetchForWriting derives the stream version from the same events it loads instead of a second read. Parallel ctx.write calls on one transaction are serialized, so a failing write rolls back only its own savepoint and no longer takes a concurrent successful write with it. ctx.notify called inside a handler reached through ctx.query is deferred onto the outer write's after-commit list instead of being delivered before that write commits. ctx.notify snapshots its options when it is called, so later mutation by the handler does not change the delivered notification. The JSDoc of AggregateStreamHandle.appendOne now states that it must not be mixed with other appends to the same aggregate in one handler.

title: registerEntityCrud merges per-verb agent hints into write.agent and read.agent
detail: agents[verb] used to replace write.agent or read.agent wholesale, so write: { agent: { expose: true } } with agents: { delete: { risk: "high" } } dropped expose on delete. The two are now merged with the per-verb value winning. An escapeHatch update/delete/restore on a row whose tenantId is not a valid TenantId throws an InternalError instead of silently appending to the operator's own tenant stream.

title: Entity list and detail handlers with escapeHatch must declare SystemAdmin-only access
detail: defineEntityListHandler, defineEntityDetailHandler and registerEntityCrud read options with escapeHatch now throw at definition unless access is { roles: ["SystemAdmin"] }, like write handlers already did. A cross-tenant read reachable by any tenant role leaked foreign rows.
migration: Give every list/detail handler that declares escapeHatch access: { roles: ["SystemAdmin"] }, or drop the escapeHatch if the handler should stay tenant-scoped.

title: Upload route creates the fileRef row in its own transaction, cleans up bytes on failure and excludes system files from unclaimedUploadReaders
detail: The file routes and the API server use createProjectingTenantDb so projections on fileRef.created run. When the row insert or a projection throws, the upload route rolls the row back, deletes the stored bytes and answers 500. Files uploaded by the system user are no longer readable through unclaimedUploadReaders.

title: Cron schedulers of a running job runner survive orphan cleanup by an older runner, and stop() waits for a timed-out boot gate
detail: The runner re-stamps its own cron schedulers in the orphan-cleanup seen hash every quarter of the grace period (one hset for all ids, cleared in stop()), so a mixed-version window longer than an hour no longer lets an older runner delete a scheduler a live runner holds. The stamps are written before the schedulers are upserted. A boot gate that exceeds its timeout is abandoned, not aborted: its handler keeps running, and stop() now waits for it (bounded) before closing connections.

title: buildServer throws at boot when a handler declares additionalRateLimits but no RateLimitResolver can be built
detail: Without a Redis client or context.rateLimit every call to such a handler (auth-email-password signup and token requests, waitlist submit) answered 500 at request time. buildServer now throws at boot and names the handlers.
migration: Wire a Redis client on context.redis (or pass context.rateLimit). For the waitlist without Redis, pass emailRateLimits: [].

title: PII backfill keeps ownerless events under the tenant key and re-keys values left under a previous owner
detail: With resolveOwnerFromProjection the projection owner is now used only when the event does not carry the owner key at all; an explicit null owner resolves through whenAbsent like the live write path. The owner re-key stage (rekeyTenantKeyedOwnerFields) also moves user-keyed values to the projection's current owner when that is another user, so after an owner change X to Y that predates re-keying on transition, forgetting Y erases the value. Known divergence: a row that went ownerless, then owned by X, then ownerless again keeps its created-event value under the tenant key, while the live path keeps it with X.

title: pruneEvents batchSize and _notifyAfterCommitFactory on the handler context
detail: pruneEvents takes an optional batchSize that deletes the lowest event ids first, so callers can loop until deletedCount is below the batch size with one short transaction per batch. The handler context exposes _notifyAfterCommitFactory, a notify factory bound to the dispatcher's job runner for use after the transaction has committed.

title: requireTierResolverPlugin narrows a tier-resolver registration or fails the boot
detail: requireTierResolverPlugin(usage) returns the TierResolverPlugin of a tenantTierResolver registration and throws "tier-resolver registration options must provide a build() factory" otherwise. runProdApp, the worker boot and runDevApp share it, so the boot error is identical in all three entry points.

title: Back-dated seed writes fail with a typed SeedTimeOrderError
detail: append() throws the exported SeedTimeOrderError (aggregateType, aggregateId, version, seedCreatedAt, predecessorCreatedAt) when a back-dated event would precede its stream predecessor, so seeders can tell it from other failures without parsing the message. The check now runs inside the insert transaction, so a concurrent live append can no longer land between check and insert.

title: kumiko-upgrade --resolve rejects --dry-run, and the installed version is found from workspace members and prerelease lockfile pins
detail: kumiko-upgrade --resolve --dry-run used to write the marker anyway; it now exits with an error and writes nothing. The installed version is now looked up from the working directory up to the repo root (the first directory with .git or a package.json with workspaces), so running inside a workspace member of a hoisted-linker monorepo finds it, while a parent workspace outside the repo is still ignored. bun.lock pins like 0.364.0-next.1 resolve to their x.y.z core instead of being dropped.

title: Non-sql index where throws instead of building a full index
detail: buildEntityTable no longer drops a malformed EntityIndexDef.where silently, which produced a full (unique) index that blocked reuse of soft-deleted values. moneyAmount is typed as a bigint column.

title: Job handlers get ctx.metricsFor like request handlers
detail: JobContext now exposes ctx.metricsFor(featureName) with the same contract as HandlerContext, so shared code can count under one stable feature name from jobs too. Unregistered names stay a silent no-op.

title: A failed scheduler seen stamp at start no longer lets an older runner remove fresh cron schedulers for good
detail: When the initial seen stamp failed, a concurrent older runner could delete the new runner's cron schedulers as orphans, and the periodic refresh only re-stamped them. The refresh now stamps and upserts the lane's cron schedulers again until both succeeded once.

title: Job runner start survives a failed scheduler-seen stamp
detail: The initial scheduler-seen stamp is best-effort like the periodic refresh and the orphan cleanup: a Redis error is logged as a warning and the runner still starts and registers its cron schedulers.

title: lockedWhen on a field with access.read fails at boot
detail: Roles that cannot read the lock field receive records without it, and the client then showed every record as locked. validateLockedWhen now rejects a lock field that declares access.read.

title: moneyAmount returns ColumnBuilder<bigint> instead of ColumnBuilder<number>
detail: The column was always created with bigint mode, so the driver returned a bigint while the type said number. The type now matches the runtime value. Code that assigned the column value to a number or did number arithmetic on it no longer typechecks.
migration: Treat values read from a moneyAmount column as bigint (for example compare with 0n, or convert explicitly with Number() where the amount is known to fit). No schema change.

title: The pdf-audit-export recipe uploads the PDF before the transaction
detail: The shipped pdf-audit-export example now renders and uploads the PDF in a beforeTransaction phase with uploadFileBytesBeforeTransaction and creates the fileRef row in the handler with createFileRefFromUploadedBytes, so the upload holds no pool connection. No runtime change.

title: The pii-personal-migration codemod skips .d.ts files in migration mode too
detail: An earlier release note said the codemod now skips .d.ts files in --report-stance mode. That mode already skipped them. What changed is that migration mode skips .d.ts files as well, matching --report-stance.

title: No false narrowing warning for where.tenantId given as { in } or { eq }
detail: The read.findOne and read.findMany steps unwrap operator-form tenant filters ({ in: [...] } and { eq }) before comparing them with the caller's tenant scope, and stay silent for operator forms they do not understand.

title: custom-handlers and tags-basic recipes follow the coding rules
detail: The custom-handlers recipe parses the detail row with Zod instead of casts and filters counter:active on the server (filter + totalCount) instead of in JS over one page. The tags-basic test isolates tests by tenant instead of raw DELETE statements. No runtime change.

title: Recipe integration tests isolate per tenant instead of raw DELETE FROM resets
detail: The recipe integration tests that agents learn from no longer reset tables with raw DELETE FROM statements. Each test now runs in its own tenant with its own users, or uses unique ids. The kumiko-schema-check header comment is now English. No runtime change.

title: Rebuilding an entity with a personal file or image field no longer fails on ciphertext from old backfill events
detail: The earlier PII backfill encrypted file and image uuid values in stored events. Replaying those created and updated events wrote the ciphertext into the uuid column and failed with invalid input syntax. applyEntityEvent now decrypts such values through the subject KMS, writes null for an erased subject, and throws a clear InternalError when no KMS is configured. Table rows were never affected because Postgres rejects the ciphertext on a uuid column.

title: SVG and HTML fragments are not resolved as application/xml
detail: For uploads without a concrete content type, markup without an XML declaration is only treated as application/xml when its root element is not a known HTML or SVG element (namespace prefixes ignored). SVG logos and HTML snippets no longer route to XML ingest providers.

title: EventStoreExecutor.restore returns a subject_erased conflict instead of throwing
detail: When the stored row has to be re-encrypted for a subject whose key was erased, restore now returns a failed WriteResult with the subject_erased ConflictError. The row stays soft-deleted and no restored event is appended. Code that called restore directly and caught the exception checks isSuccess instead.

title: Retired-table scan handles DROP TABLE lists, schema-qualified names and RENAME
detail: The scan of prior migrations for retired framework tables now marks every table in a DROP TABLE comma list as dropped, ignores a schema prefix such as "public"."table", and treats ALTER TABLE ... RENAME TO as dropping the old and creating the new name.

title: kumiko-schema status reports connection errors; kumiko-schema-check knows the scaffold layout
detail: schema status now prints a one-line error with a hint and exits 1 when the database is unreachable or missing, instead of an uncaught stacktrace (the URL is never printed). kumiko-schema-check exits 0 with a pointer to kumiko-schema validate for apps whose kumiko/schema.ts derives ENTITY_METAS from APP_FEATURES. New scaffolds create the app database in docker-compose.

title: Retention and erasure writes skip the select-option rule
detail: Framework system-user updates that name a writePurpose (retention, erasure) are no longer blocked by conditional select options. The null-clear comparison helper isUnchangedValue moved to engine/screen-helpers and is exported from ui-types so the renderer form and the executor share one definition.

title: Mid-stream token expiry returns 401 unauthenticated
detail: A stream dispatched with a token that expires while the stream is open now ends with UnauthenticatedError (401) instead of AccessDeniedError (403), so clients show the session-ended hint. Access revocation mid-stream still returns 403 access_denied.
