title: A where.tenantId of { in: [...] } or { eq } narrows TenantDb reads instead of being ignored
detail: TenantDb.readWhere only understood a plain id or an array. An operator form fell back to the full read scope (own tenant plus reference rows), so { in: [ownTenant] } still returned SYSTEM reference rows. It now unwraps { in } and { eq } with the same helper the read steps use for their narrowing warning. Ids outside the caller's scope are still dropped and never widen the read.

title: tenantlessAnonymous is blocked by an X-Tenant header only, not by the kumiko_tenant cookie
detail: An earlier release note said a tenantlessAnonymous handler never runs when the client supplies X-Tenant or kumiko_tenant. Only the X-Tenant header blocks it. An ambient kumiko_tenant cookie does not, because the tenant resolver ignores the cookie on this path anyway.

title: Test-stack rate limiting follows appContext.redis when rateLimitNowMs is set
detail: With rateLimitNowMs the test stack builds its own rate-limit resolver; it now uses the redis instance passed via the app context instead of always the internal test redis, so buckets prefilled or cleared through the app redis take effect.

title: The ZIP plausibility check picks the end record whose comment length reaches the end of the file
detail: The scan took the last end-of-central-directory signature, so a signature inside the archive comment could point the check at forged entry names. A candidate now only counts when its offset plus 22 bytes plus its comment length equals the file length. A docx upload with bytes appended after the end record is therefore rejected as content_mismatch.

title: A throwing command in a batch without a database connection releases its cap reservation
detail: The sequential fallback of dispatchBatch (no DB connection) did not release the reserved capacity when a command threw instead of returning a failure result. It now releases the reservation before rethrowing.

title: Write handlers can declare a beforeTransaction phase, and file bytes can be uploaded before the transaction
detail: defineWriteHandler accepts beforeTransaction(event, ctx), which the dispatcher runs after the pre-handler gates and any reserveBeforeTransaction and before the transaction opens, so a slow external call holds no pool connection. Its data reaches the handler as event.prepared; a failure result or throw rejects the write, and its release runs whenever the transaction does not commit. ctx.write, appendEvent, notify and the other write surfaces throw inside the phase, and a handler with the phase cannot run as a nested ctx.write. uploadFileBytesBeforeTransaction writes the bytes in that phase and createFileRefFromUploadedBytes creates the fileRef row in the handler; the release keeps the bytes when the row exists. Original files whose row never committed stay in storage, no job sweeps them.

title: Boot-validator and guard messages name the fix
detail: Boot-validator and guard messages that only described the problem now also say what to do about it. The German configEdit and retention messages are in English. Validation and guard behavior is unchanged.

title: CacheSyncBus.publish takes { remoteOnly } to skip same-process listeners
detail: `publish(topic, message, { remoteOnly: true })` delivers only to other processes. Use it when the publisher has already applied the change locally and a local fanout would trigger a redundant reload.

title: changes.json no longer ships paths into private repositories
detail: Older changelog entries named file paths and a docs path of private repositories. They now name only the repository. The changelog guard rejects a `<private-repo>/<path>` reference or a github.com link into a private repository.

title: coerceRow no longer claims the raw driver row already has the converted shape
detail: coerceRow now accepts a Record<string, unknown> driver row and returns the explicitly requested row type, with the single cast at that boundary. The raw event-consumer, pending-event and projection-rebuild queries return untyped rows instead of a caller-chosen generic. The eventMigrations JSDoc and the expand/contract guide now state that pii and encrypted fields reach transforms as field-bound ciphertext and must not be renamed or derived from.

title: collectTableMetas rejects two features registering the same table name
detail: Two entities or storeTables with the same table name produced duplicate metas that only failed later in `schema generate` with a message about a hand-added meta. collectTableMetas now throws at the first registration with both origins, so setupTestStack fails the same way. The duplicate-name error of the migration generator no longer assumes a hand-added meta.

title: System-cron escape hatch audits are deduplicated per target and repeat daily
detail: The per-process dedup of declared system-cron hatches keyed only on handler, kind and tenant, so a run writing several global tables was audited for the first table only, and a worker running longer than the audit retention left no event. The key now includes the target and the process audits again after 24 hours.

title: A detail() cache hit with an ownership predicate costs one database statement
detail: The ownership re-check and the live stream-version read for a cached detail row now run as a single query, so a cache hit is no more expensive than a cache miss for entities with SQL ownership rules.

title: A later cookieDomain or secureCookies:false no longer leaves stale __Host- auth and csrf cookies behind
detail: expireLegacySessionCookieVariants covers both directions. With unprefixed names and secure cookies, setAuthCookies and clearSessionCookies now also expire __Host-kumiko_auth and __Host-kumiko_csrf as Secure, Path=/, host-only. Before, the browser kept sending the stale __Host-kumiko_csrf in X-CSRF-Token and every write failed with csrf_token_mismatch until it expired.

title: Expired fileRef purge no longer stalls on rows that keep failing
detail: The soft-delete cleanup always selected the oldest 500 expired fileRefs, so 500 permanently failing rows (unsafe key, missing list permission) blocked every newer expired fileRef of that tenant. A run now walks the expired rows page by page along (deletedAt, id) and ends on an empty page; failed rows are retried on the next run.

title: Extra routes outside /api get the request body cap for every entry
detail: extraRoutes with entry anonymous or user outside /api now run behind the maxRequestBytes body limit like signature routes already did, so an unauthenticated caller can no longer stream an oversized body into a public form or callback route.

title: FileContext.refFromFileRef reads files whose fileRef moved to another tenant
detail: A tenant handover moves the fileRef row but not the bytes, so the storageKey keeps the previous tenant's prefix and the tenant-bound `ctx.files.ref(key)` rejected it. FileContext gains `refFromFileRef({ storageKey })` for keys read from a fileRef row the caller has already tenant-checked: it skips the tenant-prefix check and still rejects unsafe keys. The variant route and ctx.derivatives.variant use it, so variants of handed-over files render again. `ref(key)` keeps the prefix check for freely supplied keys.

title: A save with file fields loads its fileRef rows once
detail: The tenant check and the pending-upload binding of a save each read every named fileRef row inside the write transaction. They now share one query over the ids, restricted to the writer's tenant and live rows. Values that are not UUIDs are still skipped.

title: Agent guide and generated indexes ship in the framework package
detail: The framework package now contains AGENTS.md plus an agents/ directory with generated feature, widget and example indexes, built from feature-manifest.json, the renderer-web exports and samples/recipes. The new agent-docs-drift guard in kumiko check fails when the committed files differ from the generator output. New apps get an AGENTS.md and a CLAUDE.md that point at the packaged guide.

title: Handler field references support business keys and array fields
migration: handlerFieldReference(schema, field) now returns { entity, by, multiple } instead of the entity string. Replace reference with reference.entity; skip or handle fields where by is set (value is a business key, not an id) or multiple is true (value is an array).

title: An empty jsonText match list no longer returns every row
detail: A where filter `{ jsonText: [] }` on a jsonb column used to add no condition, so the query returned all rows. It now matches no rows, like `in: []`. A `null` or non-object entry in the list throws the descriptive jsonText error instead of a bare TypeError.

title: Facet field docs name the reference exception
detail: The docs of projectionList.facets and relatedList.facets said every facet field must be a declared column. A facet of type "reference" is exempt: it filters by id through the bound query's filters and needs a registered entity instead. Behavior is unchanged.

title: list() reads rows and stream versions in one statement
detail: The entity list read the rows first and the stream versions in a second statement, so a concurrent write could pair old row data with a newer version, and an update built on that version would pass the optimistic lock. The stream version is now a correlated subquery of the list statement, the same way detail() reads it.

title: Existing tenant indexes pick up searchable fields added to the registry default
detail: The lazy default configuration now also applies to an index whose stored searchable, filterable and sortable attributes are a strict subset of the current default (an older default after a deploy added fields). Indexes holding any attribute outside the current default are treated as an explicit configure() and stay untouched, as before.

title: Writes without an open transaction run as their own command; ctx.db writes there throw
detail: Write handlers accept transaction "perCommand". Such a handler runs without a transaction of its own, so every ctx.write and ctx.writeAs it issues runs as its own top-level command with its own transaction, gates and afterCommit hooks. A perCommand handler cannot run as a nested ctx.write, cannot be part of a multi-command batch (422 per_command_handler_in_batch) and cannot combine with beforeTransaction or reserveBeforeTransaction (boot error). ctx.write and ctx.writeAs from stream handlers and top-level query handlers now take the same route, so afterCommit hooks of the called write, which never fired before, fire now. ctx.db writes (entity executor, insertOne, updateMany, deleteMany, db.global() writes) and event appends (appendEvent, unsafeAppendEvent, tryAppendEvent, fetchForWriting, archiveStream, restoreStream, snapshotAggregate) throw in stream handlers, top-level query handlers, perCommand handlers and in beforeTransaction and reserveBeforeTransaction. ctx.dbOutsideTransaction and ctx.outsideTransaction stay available, and ctx.db.unsafeRaw stays open as the audited escape hatch.
migration: Stream and query code that writes through ctx.db or an executor bound to ctx.db calls a write handler through ctx.write or ctx.writeAs instead, or writes deliberately through ctx.dbOutsideTransaction. Check code that relied on afterCommit hooks of a write called from a stream or query handler not firing. bookCapUsage from a stream or query handler needs outsideTransaction true or a command. runInOwnTransaction(ctx.db, ...) stays locked in these contexts; runInOwnTransaction(ctx.dbOutsideTransaction, ...) is the way to a deliberate own transaction. Measured consumers: one stream handler (AI agent turn: conversation, activity and tool-call records through an executor on ctx.db, plus cap booking) and one query handler (AI text run: cap booking on ctx.db, log via ctx.write). No other consumer app has stream or query writes. The beforeTransaction/reserveBeforeTransaction lock affects no released code.

title: decryptForRead and eager-loaded refs decrypt file, image, files and images fields that hold legacy ciphertext
detail: Only the encrypt side skips file-reference fields. The decrypt side uses collectPiiSubjectFields again and passes plaintext through unchanged, so rows written by the old backfill, which encrypted the file uuid, are read as plaintext instead of failing with pii_ciphertext_leak.

title: Cascade deletes honour the record-lock exemptions and ignore soft-deleted children
detail: The cascade hook blocked a parent delete on a locked child even when the executor delete had skipped the lock guard (unsafeSkipLockGuard, a framework system write with a writePurpose, forget). DeleteContext now carries lockGuardBypassed and the hook follows it. Soft-deleted children no longer count as locked.

title: reserveBeforeTransaction contexts now reject writes that would escape the transaction
detail: The context passed to reserveBeforeTransaction now throws on ctx.write, writeAs, event appends, scheduleAfterCommit, notify and jobRunner, like the beforeTransaction phase does. dbOutsideTransaction, outsideTransaction and forTenant stay available because reservations deliberately write outside the transaction.

title: Restore no longer writes plaintext PII from pre-KMS rows into the event log
detail: Restore now decrypts the soft-deleted row and re-encrypts it like delete before storing previous, so rows written before the subject KMS was configured no longer leak plaintext personal fields into the restored event. Restoring such a row for an erased subject now fails like delete.

title: bindReferencedFiles binds only refs of the record's tenant in one bulk load
detail: File refs for a page are loaded with a single query restricted to the writer's tenant and live rows; system-owned refs are not bound to records.

title: Boot validator covers option, prefill, emptyState, anonymous rate-limit and searchable-access gaps
detail: Rejects optionsQuery combined with optionsAvailabilityQuery, invalid dashboard valueFormat kinds, from-today panels without ranges or brush, params on emptyState navigate/drawer, unknown submitPrefilled keys, per-user rate limits on tenantless anonymous handlers, unknown conditional select option values, and searchable fields (including embedded sub-fields) the reader cannot access.

title: Malformed requestId or batch command shapes return 400 instead of failing later
detail: The dispatch and batch routes parse requestId and each command before dispatching, returning a validation error for malformed shapes, and the JSON body reader no longer relies on a type assertion.

title: files/images maxCount is validated on write
detail: The generated write schema applies .max(maxCount) to files and images fields, so payloads with more ids than allowed are rejected with a validation error.

title: render/parse roundtrip keeps secrets valid when writeRoles is empty
detail: renderSecret and renderSecretNamespace omit writeRoles when the list is empty so the rendered source parses back to the same definition.

title: A stale auth cookie on the SSE stream ends the web session with a session-ended frame
detail: With anonymousAccess, a stale or revoked auth cookie downgrades /api/sse to an anonymous 200, so the web client never noticed the session end and live updates stopped silently. The stream now opens with a session-ended frame carrying the rejection code and expires the auth cookies; the renderer-web live-events client calls onSessionEnded once for it.

title: Unit tests no longer leak a console.warn spy into later files
detail: The search payload precedence tests spy on console.warn per test and restore it, so later files in the same --no-isolate worker start with the real console.warn. The mail editor missing-language test waits for the placeholder rail instead of reading it before the validate query settled.

title: Calling transaction() on a tx or savepoint handle fails with an InternalError
detail: `RawClient.begin` is now typed optional, and `transaction()` checks it like `runInNewTransaction` does, so a nested call raises an InternalError ("runner has no begin()") instead of a TypeError. The migrate runner requires `begin` on its client and rejects handles without it before running any SQL.

title: Fewer unchecked casts in bundled features, dev-server, server-runtime, testing and cli
detail: Casts are replaced by shared type guards, typed query rows and direct Bun typings. Behavior stays the same, except that a tier-resolver registration without a build() factory now fails with a clear error at boot, the kumiko CLI prints the thrown value of non-Error failures instead of "undefined".

title: Remove unknown cast-boundary reasons and share propertyOf
detail: Framework internals read untyped properties through the shared propertyOf from kumiko-types instead of private copies and casts. The as-casts guard knows four more boundary reasons (phantom-brand, third-party-type-gap, dom-event-target, feature-exports) and normalizes whitespace in cast targets so re-indenting a multi-line cast no longer counts as a regression. A stored inbound-mail cursor that is not a JSON object is now treated like a missing cursor.

title: ctx.notify in write handlers delivers after commit
detail: Inside a write handler's transaction ctx.notify only records the notification and delivers it once the write has committed, so a rolled-back write sends nothing and leaves no attempt event. Delivery no longer takes a connection from the app pool while the write holds one, which deadlocked at pool max N with N parallel writes. With immediate: true the call stays synchronous and runs its DB work on the outside-transaction pool.
migration: NotifyResult is now a union, NotifyDispatched ({ kind: "dispatched", deliveries }) or NotifyDeferred ({ kind: "deferred" }). In a write handler without immediate: true ctx.notify returns deferred and delivers after commit (a rollback means no notification). Code that reads the result (for example a "send test message" handler showing sent/failed) sets immediate: true, which delivers synchronously on the outside-transaction pool and returns dispatched; narrow on kind before reading deliveries. Errors such as a missing idempotency Redis, a tenant broadcast without the tenant feature or an unknown notification type no longer throw in a deferred write handler, they land in the afterCommit log. Notifications from jobs, from seeding and from handlers without a transaction stay synchronous. The boot default wires tenantUserIdsQuery for to: { tenant } when the tenant feature is mounted, so an app-side tenantUserIdsQuery wiring can go. Custom NotifyFactory implementations receive an optional 4th parameter deliveryDb, and DeliveryService.notify an optional 6th.

title: Shared type guards and fewer unchecked casts in framework internals
detail: "@cosmicdrift/kumiko-types/type-guards" exports isPlainObject, isOneOf and errorCodeOf. The framework replaces many unchecked as-casts with narrowing, generic query rows and table-introspection helpers. encryptPiiFieldValues is generic over the row and returns PiiEncryptedRow<TRow>, so callers read encrypted fields without casts. Behavior stays the same.

title: r.notification declares variables, template and meta; applyBootSeeds seeds them
detail: r.notification accepts variables (typed with templateVariable.text, link, money, date and list), template (per locale body, document html) and meta (per locale subject and more). Boot validation requires a kebab-case name, a meta.<locale>.subject for every template locale and valid placeholder names. templateVariablesToZod turns the variables into a Zod schema. applyBootSeeds calls seedNotificationTemplates, which writes the text as system templates of kind mail and fails loudly when notifications declare a template but the template-resolver feature is not mounted.

title: r.notification works without trigger and ships localized templates
detail: trigger, recipient and data are optional and must be declared together, a notification without trigger is sent explicitly through ctx.notify. localizedTemplate groups body and meta per locale and is mutually exclusive with template and meta. The variable names link, money and date are reserved for template helpers. ctx.notify validates the data against the declared variables and fails the write on a missing required variable. New exports are listMailLocales, hasMailTranslationKey, assertNotificationVariables and NotificationLocalizedTemplate.

title: ctx.notify rejects a broadcast to another tenant
detail: A notify with to: { tenant } now throws an AccessDeniedError (reason notify_foreign_tenant_broadcast) unless the tenant is the caller's own, before any delivery work. In a write handler it fails synchronously instead of landing in the afterCommit log. Notifications fired from seed hooks during self-signup no longer use the app pool inside the signup transaction, which deadlocked at pool max N with N parallel signups; they deliver after commit. ctx.scheduleAfterCommit is now absent in query bridges and post-commit contexts, where hooks pushed to it never ran; callers that check for it (cache-sync announce, set-tenant-tier onAssigned, form-draft discard, seed hooks) now run inline there instead of being dropped.
migration: to: { tenant } must be the tenant of the caller (user.tenantId of the handler or job context), otherwise notify throws; in a write handler the throw is synchronous. Seed-hook notifications in the signup transaction run after commit and return { kind: "deferred" } (immediate: true runs synchronously on the outside-transaction pool, which cannot see rows the signup transaction has not committed yet, so a tenant broadcast there finds no new member). No known consumer broadcasts to a foreign tenant.

title: Client schema carries entity lockedWhen
detail: buildAppSchema projects lockedWhen, so an entityEdit screen shows a locked record read-only without a screen-level readOnly.

title: r.secret options with function values (redact) no longer fail to parse
detail: r.secret(...) options that contain arrow or function expressions (for example redact: () => "••••••••") were reported as "options could not be read as a plain object", which turned the whole feature into a legacy corpus entry. The functions are now kept verbatim as raw references, option keys stay visible and a parse to render round-trip keeps them (multi-line function bodies may be re-indented). Function values in other patterns (entity, nav, metric, job) are still rejected on purpose.
migration: Consumers that ship a checked-in few-shot corpus (Enterprise) should regenerate it on the next framework bump; its drift test enforces that.

title: Binding of referenced files only for the record creator's own uploads
detail: files:write:bind-referenced-files now binds a file only if the record creator uploaded it (or the system generated it), so foreign references cannot expose private uploads.

title: files:write:bind-referenced-files binds a record's referenced files
detail: System-only handler that binds the files a record references through its declared file fields (legacy uploads with entityId null, records created without a save lifecycle) so record readers can open them. Skips files bound elsewhere, of another tenant or missing. Callable from es-ops seeds via ctx.systemWriteAs; pages with limit and nextAfterId.

title: Optional number fields in entity forms start empty instead of 0
migration: An optional number field without default no longer starts at 0 in entityEdit create/edit, and an untouched one is not sent. If a screen relied on the implicit 0, declare default: 0 on the field.

title: unclaimedUploadReaders option for createFilesFeature
detail: Roles listed in unclaimedUploadReaders may read (not delete) uploads that have no entityType and entityId, for documents referenced without a file field.

title: Query handlers may declare personalData public-intake
detail: The personal-data write gate computed the public-intake exemption only for write handlers, so an anonymous query handler that wrote personal data (directly or through a nested write) was always rejected, and the boot validator refused access.personalData on query handlers. Query handlers now follow the same rules as write handlers: access.personalData "public-intake" requires the anonymous role and an active rateLimit (not disabled). openToAll.personalData stays write-only, stream handlers still cannot declare personalData.
migration: No consumer change; anonymous query handlers that write personal data now declare access.personalData: "public-intake" instead of failing at the write gate.

title: Boot check for edit field prefill
detail: validateBoot allows today only on date fields, currentUser displayName and email only on text fields and id on text or reference fields.

title: Boot check for the entityEdit readOnly condition
detail: validateBoot rejects a screen readOnly condition whose field is not a field of the screen's entity.

title: Boot check for embeddedList on edit fields
detail: validateBoot requires the field to be an embedded list and every readOnlyCells entry to be a sub-field.

title: Locked records reject executor writes
detail: The event-store executor checks entity.lockedWhen against the loaded row in update and delete and fails with RecordLockedError (409, code record_locked, i18n key errors.recordLocked); a missing condition field counts as locked. Create, restore, forget, framework-system-user writes that name a writePurpose and the write that sets the lock pass. validateBoot rejects a lockedWhen field that is unknown, personal, encrypted or not a plain scalar type.

title: POST /files checks write access to the target record
detail: createRecordWriteCheck loads the stored row tenant-scoped and applies update-handler access, entity access.write, field write access and lockedWhen before the upload is stored. Results map to 404, 403 and 409 record_locked. Uploads with an entityId and no check wired are refused.
migration: Grant the uploader the entity's update right for records they attach files to, or upload without an entityId and bind the file on save. Entities without a generic :update handler no longer accept uploads with an entityId. Code that used entityId as a free slot without a stored record must create the record first.

title: Unbound uploads are private to the uploader (security)
detail: The default file access guard denies every operation on a file with no entityType or no entityId unless the caller is the uploader or has a role in privilegedRoles; the file routes answer 404 as for any denied file. Before, files without entityType were readable by the whole tenant and pending uploads until a record claimed them. bindPendingFileRefs now also runs for updates and binds the file ids named in the update's changes for file, image, files and images fields (same entityType and fieldName, entityId null, insertedById = caller), so createFileRefFromBytes with attachTo but no entityId plus a following update write attaches the file to the record.
migration: Code that shows a file without entityType to other users (tenant logo, avatar, mail attachment, import preview, AI-agent output) must upload it with entityType and fieldName of a file field on a record and save the record, so readers of that record can read it; or keep it uploader-only, run the read as a role in privilegedRoles, or set a custom accessGuard in the files feature options. Apps that set accessGuard keep their own decision. Code that reads another user's pending upload before the record is saved must bind the file first or run as the uploader. Known case: solon's document upload posts without entityType and the later document record (created by the ingest job, not the uploader) stores the id in its `fileId` field, so other users no longer read the original; solon must upload with entityType and fieldName of `fileId` and bind the file when the record is created, because a different creator cannot claim the pending upload.

title: Personal file/image fields are no longer encrypted
detail: collectPiiSubjectFields still lists file, image, files and images fields with a personal annotation (forget and retention use it), but the new collectPiiEncryptedFields leaves them out and every encrypt, decrypt, backfill and store-gate path now uses it. The column holds only the fileRef uuid; the binary is erased by the file-ref user-data hook.

title: Personal fields are re-keyed to the new owner on owner change
detail: On absent to X and X to Y, the executor writes the personal fields (personal: { of: ownerField }) of the row under the new owner's key into the update event, so the projection, a rebuild and every event from the transition on agree and only the current owner's forget decides erasure. As a result <entity>.updated changes can contain personal fields the caller did not send. X to absent keeps the values under X so the last owner's forget still erases them. The created event from before an owner existed stays tenant-keyed in the immutable log. The new backfill option rekeyTenantKeyedOwnerFields moves such tenant-keyed values under the owner the projection or payload names (never via whenAbsent, a projection row of another tenant is ignored, other tenants' keys are not touched, a forgotten owner yields the erased sentinel). The boot PII backfill passes it, and its fingerprint now includes a transform version, so each deployment runs one full pass and afterwards only catch-up passes near the cursor. A created event whose owner transition happens after that full pass is not rescanned and stays tenant-keyed until someone runs backfillEventPiiEncryption(db, registry, { resolveOwnerFromProjection: true, rekeyTenantKeyedOwnerFields: true }) followed by a projection rebuild, or the transform version is bumped.
migration: No consumer code change. The boot backfill runs in the background (startPiiEventBackfillOnBoot, it does not block readiness, KUMIKO_SKIP_PII_BACKFILL=1 turns it off). On the first boot after the bump it does one full scan of kumiko_events and rebuilds the affected projections. Consumers reading updated.changes must not treat a personal field there as a user edit when the owner field changed in the same event.

title: Plural file fields have a projection column
detail: files and images fields get a jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]' column on the entity table (entity-table-meta, buildEntityTable row type readonly string[]) and applyEntityEvent no longer strips them from updated events. Detail and list queries return the ordered id arrays; before, they never carried the field, so an edit form of a saved record showed no files. kumiko schema generate emits an in-place ADD COLUMN for existing tables and no .rebuild.json, so existing rows hold [] until their projection is rebuilt from the events.
migration: Run kumiko schema generate and apply the migration. Existing rows keep [] until the entity projection is rebuilt, so add a rebuild marker before applying: create <NNNN_migration-name>.rebuild.json next to the generated SQL with {"version":1,"tables":["<table name from the ALTER TABLE statement>"]}; kumiko schema apply then rebuilds the projection. Without the marker, call enqueueProjectionRebuild("<feature>:projection:<entity>-entity", { db, registry, jobRunner }) from @cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/migrations once per entity. Known consumers: solon protocol (attachmentFileIds) and the Wartungs-Demo (photos). Code that read the ids of a plural file field from the event log or from file_refs can read the row field instead.

title: Files removed from a record are deleted
detail: disposeRemovedFileRefs runs next to bindPendingFileRefs for every save that is not a create. For each file field named in changes it soft-deletes the fileRefs present in previous but not in the saved row, when entityType, entityId and fieldName match this record. The binary is removed by the soft-delete cleanup job after retention, or by forget.

title: Schema generate rejects a table listed twice in ENTITY_METAS
detail: When ENTITY_METAS contained the same tableName twice, the migration diff kept only the last definition and compared it against the previous snapshot entry, so a new index was written to .snapshot.json but no CREATE INDEX reached the migration SQL. kumiko-schema generate, kumiko-schema validate and programmatic generateMigration now throw (generate and validate exit 1 with a message naming every duplicated table) before any file is written.
migration: Remove hand-added metas for tables a feature already registers from kumiko/schema.ts. Known: phronexsis's schema file appends IN_APP_MESSAGES_META next to collectTableMetas(FEATURES); drop it (and its comment), then run kumiko-schema generate — the existing in_app_messages_tenant_user_created_idx comes out as CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS (no-op) and the two legacy indexes as commented review drops. The duplicate in_app_messages entry in .snapshot.json disappears with that generate.

title: Soft-delete cleanup removes the bytes of expired fileRefs
detail: softDeleteCleanupJob handles the fileRef entity through purgeExpiredFileRefsWithBytes, which deletes the original and its derivatives via the file provider and then only the rows whose bytes are gone. Failures are logged and retried on the next run.

title: setupTestStack option lifecycleSystemHooks
detail: Passes the given SystemHooks to buildServer, so tests can exercise pipeline lifecycle hooks like createCascadeDeleteHook through the real HTTP stack.

title: Writes with file ids from another tenant are rejected
detail: A create or update that puts a file id into a file or image field now fails with a ValidationError (code invalid_element, path = field name) when the id is not a UUID, does not exist, or belongs to another tenant. That includes files stored under the SYSTEM tenant. On update only the changed fields are checked. The check runs for every write that returns a save result, inside the transaction, before pending file refs are bound. System users created for a tenant pass with that tenant's own files.
migration: Check seeds, imports and handlers that copy file ids across tenants or reference files uploaded as SYSTEM. Upload the file in the target tenant (or copy it there) before writing its id. A custom handler that writes through an executor directly, without returning a save result, is not covered and needs its own check.

title: Secure host-only session cookies use the __Host- prefix
detail: Auth, csrf and tenant cookies are named __Host-kumiko_auth, __Host-kumiko_csrf and __Host-kumiko_tenant when they are written Secure and without a Domain (the tenant cookie is always host-only). With auth.cookieDomain or without Secure the auth and csrf names stay kumiko_auth and kumiko_csrf. New auth option secureCookies forces Secure (default NODE_ENV === "production"). Login deletes the legacy unprefixed host-only cookies, logout and deleteTenantCookie delete the prefixed and the legacy names. The server reads only the resolved names, so a request that carries only the legacy kumiko_auth is anonymous. AUTH_COOKIE_NAME, CSRF_COOKIE_NAME and TENANT_COOKIE_NAME are removed from the framework and dispatcher-live; the base names and sessionCookieName() are exported from @cosmicdrift/kumiko-types/session-cookies and @cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/api, getSessionCookies(c) returns the resolved names of a request. The testing package's CSRF_COOKIE_NAME stays and resolves to the unprefixed name (e2e servers run without Secure).
migration: Every user logs in once after the deploy, because the old kumiko_auth cookie is no longer read. Custom clients, proxies or scripts that read or forward the cookies by literal name break: read the names through sessionCookieName() / resolveSessionCookieNames() (types package) or getSessionCookies(c) on the server, and handle both the prefixed and the plain name in browser code (readCsrfToken() already does). Replace imports of AUTH_COOKIE_NAME, CSRF_COOKIE_NAME and TENANT_COOKIE_NAME with AUTH_COOKIE_BASE, CSRF_COOKIE_BASE and TENANT_COOKIE_BASE plus sessionCookieName(); e2e helpers that imported CSRF_COOKIE_NAME from @cosmicdrift/kumiko-dispatcher-live import it from @cosmicdrift/kumiko-testing/e2e instead (known: solon's e2e helpers and specs, and a kumiko-enterprise integration test that uses AUTH_COOKIE_NAME). A reverse proxy that strips or rewrites cookie names must pass the __Host- names unchanged. Staging or preview deployments over plain http need no change (Secure is off there); set auth.secureCookies (also accepted by runProdApp) explicitly when TLS terminates before the app and NODE_ENV is not "production". A standalone createAuthRoutes mount outside buildServer must also mount sessionCookiesMiddleware with the same resolved names, otherwise the readers fall back to the domain-less default.

title: Duplicate session cookie names end the cookie session
detail: When the Cookie header carries the resolved auth or csrf cookie name more than once, authMiddleware ignores the cookie transport and expires every variant (prefixed host-only, legacy host-only, the cookieDomain variant and retired domains). With anonymousAccess the request continues as anonymous, otherwise it gets 401 missing_token; a Bearer token on the same request still authenticates. A prefixed and a legacy name side by side are not a duplicate. The cookie clearing moved from the auth routes into clearSessionCookies in session-cookies.ts; ResolvedSessionCookies carries domain and retiredDomains.

title: Origin guard defaults on when the public app URL is known
detail: New auth option publicOrigin. Without allowedOrigins, cookieDomain and unsafeSkipOriginCheck, buildServer mounts the Origin guard for cookie-authenticated state-changing /api requests and admits publicOrigin plus the request's own host (Host header). runProdApp sets publicOrigin from auth.publicOrigin, then auth.mail.baseUrl, then the APP_BASE_URL env (origin only, path dropped); with none of them in production it logs a warning that the Origin guard is off and boots anyway. allowedOrigins keeps its strict meaning, and the WebSocket check and the anonymous downgrade still use only allowedOrigins.
migration: Cookie-authenticated POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE requests from a page on another origin than the public app URL and than the API host itself now get 403 origin_not_allowed in runProdApp deployments that set auth.mail.baseUrl or APP_BASE_URL. A web client served from a different host than the API (for example a sibling subdomain) must list its origin in auth.allowedOrigins. Same-host setups, custom domains served by the same server and Bearer clients need no change.

title: createFileRefFromBytes creates FileRefs from handler- or job-produced bytes
detail: createFileRefFromBytes({ db, files, registry, user }, { fileName, mimeType, data, attachTo? }) shares one pipeline with POST /api/files, so identifier checks, field-level maxSize/accept, content sniffing, MIME resolution, the tenant-prefixed storage key and the fileRef.created event are identical. The tenant always comes from ctx.user. A rejected file returns a 422 write failure with reason file_rejected and the upload error string in details.error. The FileRef's insertedById is the passed user, so the default access guard lets only that user and privileged roles read files attached to an entity.

title: Cron jobs with an IANA time zone, images fields with capture
detail: A cron trigger accepts tz (IANA name; without it the server process zone applies) and is scheduled in that zone, DST included. r.job() throws at boot for an invalid zone. createImagesField accepts capture ("environment" | "user") like createImageField, and the edit view model carries it for images fields.

title: Uploads from an update form are attached to the record
detail: computeEditViewModel accepts entityId (the record being edited, update mode only) and sets it on the hints of file, image, files and images fields; RenderEdit passes the id it was mounted with and the file input sends it as the entityId multipart part of POST /api/files. Create forms send no entityId; after a successful create the write pipeline binds the caller's own pending uploads named in the record's file fields (same entityType and fieldName, entityId null, insertedById = caller) to the new record via a fileRef.updated event in the same transaction, for single and plural file fields alike, when the files feature (fileRef entity) is mounted. Behaviour change: such files are now attached to the record. The default file access guard allows read on an attached file to the uploader, privilegedRoles (default Admin/SystemAdmin) and everyone whose run of the entity's <entity>:detail query returns the record; delete stays uploader and privilegedRoles only. A qr-overlay variant of an image field no longer throws for a file uploaded from an update or create form. Write-form sections send no entityId. EmbeddedListInput has a new required actionsLabel prop.
migration: Files attached through forms now follow the record's read access instead of being tenant-wide: anyone who cannot read the record no longer reads the file, anyone who can read it does. Check image, images, file and files fields whose files must be visible beyond the record's readers (for example an avatar shown in lists to users without detail access) and add those roles to privilegedRoles or set accessGuard in the files feature options. An entity without a detail query falls back to uploader plus privilegedRoles. Files uploaded before the update keep their old attachment. Custom primitive sets that implement EmbeddedListInput accept the new actionsLabel prop and render it as the actions column header; custom file/image Input primitives forward entityId into the upload and offer a remove control that calls onChange(null).

title: images and files fields get an edit widget; required is allowed
detail: NO_WIDGET_FIELD_TYPES now holds only jsonb and embedded. required true on an images or files field passes boot validation and the client-side check treats an empty array as missing. The edit view model carries maxCount for files and images fields.

title: actionForm screens honour the called handler's excludedFields
detail: buildAppSchema projects the handler's excludedFields onto actionForm screens as writeExcludedFields (a flat list, unlike entityEdit's per-verb object). The form shows these fields read-only, not required and never in the payload.
migration: Drop a hand-written readOnly lock on an actionForm field once the handler it calls declares excludedFields for it.

title: useExtension options with function values and package-imported extension names no longer fail to parse
detail: r.useExtension(...) options that contain arrow or function expressions (for example isPublic: ({ entityId }) => ...) were reported as "options could not be read as a plain object", which turned the whole feature into a legacy corpus entry. The functions are now kept verbatim as raw references, option keys stay visible and parse to render round-trips unchanged. An extension name imported from a package whose types resolve to dist/*.d.ts (an installed @cosmicdrift/* package in a consumer repo) is now read from its `export declare const NAME: "value"` type instead of failing. Function values elsewhere (entity, nav, metric, job) are still rejected on purpose.
migration: Consumers that ship a checked-in few-shot corpus (Enterprise) should regenerate it on the next framework bump; its drift test enforces that. The new ratchet test in dev-server pins the framework's own canonical count and parse-error ceiling.

title: Job runner removes job schedulers of cron jobs that no longer exist
detail: When an app drops a cron job, its BullMQ job scheduler stayed in Redis and kept firing, so the worker logged `Unknown job` on every tick. On start, each lane now removes every scheduler in its own queue that does not belong to a registered cron job of that lane (logged per removal). Each runner records when it last upserted a scheduler; a scheduler outside the runner's own set is only removed if it was not upserted within the last hour, so an old pod restarting during a rolling deploy does not delete the scheduler of a cron job the new version just added. Schedulers with no record, such as the old colon-form ids, are removed right away. A failing cleanup is logged as a warning and does not stop the start. This replaces the dedicated removal of the old colon-form scheduler ids.

title: Outside-transaction access no longer deadlocks against the write pool
detail: ctx.dbOutsideTransaction, ctx.systemDb.outsideTransaction and ctx.outsideTransaction used the same pool as the handler's own transaction. With as many concurrent writes as pool slots, each write held a connection and waited for a second one, so every request hung forever. They now use a dedicated pool (DispatcherOptions.outsideTransactionDb) sized by the new DATABASE_OUTSIDE_TX_POOL_MAX (default 3). runProdApp and the worker boot also read DATABASE_POOL_MAX, DATABASE_POOL_IDLE_TIMEOUT and DATABASE_POOL_CONNECT_TIMEOUT now; before, production ignored them and used the postgres.js default of 10.
migration: Each pod now opens up to DATABASE_POOL_MAX + DATABASE_OUTSIDE_TX_POOL_MAX connections (defaults 10 + 3) plus the LISTEN connection; check the total against Postgres max_connections, including rolling-update surge. A set but invalid DATABASE_POOL_MAX, DATABASE_POOL_IDLE_TIMEOUT, DATABASE_POOL_CONNECT_TIMEOUT or DATABASE_OUTSIDE_TX_POOL_MAX now aborts the boot. Hand-built dispatchers can pass outsideTransactionDb in DispatcherOptions; without it the app pool is shared as before.

title: Entity PII fields need whenAbsent: "tenant" when the owner field is nullable
detail: personal: { of: "<owner>", whenAbsent: "tenant" } makes rows without an owner editable, deletable and forgettable with an active KMS, without plaintext PII. The subject is resolved in this order: the owner on the previous row, the owner the same event sets, then the tenant key (tenant:<tenantId>). Before, an update, delete or forget of an ownerless row failed with SubjectResolutionError (HTTP 500) once a KMS was configured. backfill-pii follows the same chain and checks the projection row for the owner before it falls back to the tenant key; an updated event whose previous.owner is null but whose changes.owner is set no longer loses the owner. Entity fields have no plaintext fallback, so "tenant" is the only value. bundled jobs: cron and system runs (triggeredById null) now store payload, error and log messages as ciphertext under the system tenant key instead of plaintext.
migration: Boot now aborts for a personal: { of: "<owner>" } field whose owner field is not required and that declares no whenAbsent: [Feature X] Field "f" on entity "e" is personal: { of: "ownerId" }, but "ownerId" is not required — rows without an owner would fail to encrypt (SubjectResolutionError, HTTP 500) on update, delete and forget. Declare { personal: { of: "ownerId", whenAbsent: "tenant" } } to encrypt those rows under the tenant key, or make "ownerId" required: true. Entity fields have no plaintext fallback (fw#3654). Fix: add whenAbsent: "tenant", or make the owner field required: true if every row has one. whenAbsent on personal: { of: "id" } throws at declaration. Known consumers: kumiko-enterprise (entities with an ownerUserId, authorId or ownerId owner field) and offlot-app (a lead entity with enquiryId). Existing plaintext job-run rows of cron runs stay readable; new ones are ciphertext.

title: Executor update accepts includeDeleted for soft-deleted rows
detail: `executor.update(payload, user, db, { includeDeleted: true })` loads the row without the soft-delete filter (the tenant filter stays), so server code can move a trashed row together with its parent (for example a team change) and a later restore lands consistently. The row stays deleted. The default is unchanged (NotFound) and the generic HTTP update handler never sets the option. The projection apply was already unfiltered by `isDeleted`, so live and rebuild agree. The search consumer treats an update on a soft-deleted row as a removal, so the moved row does not reappear in search.

title: Boot validation covers multiSelect optionsAvailabilityQuery on entity and screen fields
Executor create accepts streamTenantId; ctx.forTenant(tenantId) for gated cross-tenant writes
detail: createEventStoreExecutor().create takes { streamTenantId } (stream, event tenant, row tenant, PII key and cache invalidation follow it, the acting user stays the operator). The override is accepted on a system-mode db and also on a tenant-mode db bound to exactly that stream tenant. New handler-context method ctx.forTenant(tenantId) returns { db, streamTenantId }: a tenant-mode db bound to the target tenant plus the stream override to pass to the executor, so a handler needs no unsafeRaw escape hatch for cross-tenant writes. A foreign tenant is gated to SystemAdmin and system identities (AccessDeniedError with reason tenant_override_requires_system_admin otherwise); the caller's own tenant returns streamTenantId undefined. It is not offered to r.systemScope() handlers. The bundled cross-tenant handlers (tenant removeMember/updateMemberRoles, tier setTenantTier, custom-fields system fields, template-resolver upserts/set, managed-pages set, compliance-profiles setProfile) no longer rewrite event.user.tenantId; the event actor is the operator. tenant cancelPendingInvitation takes an optional streamTenantId.

title: Job ctx.queryAs is gated like ctx.writeAs
migration: Jobs calling ctx.queryAs with createSystemUser(...) or any identity other than the job's own caller now fail with AccessDeniedError (system_identity_switch_denied / identity_switch_denied). Declare r.systemScope() on the job's feature or escapeHatch: { reason } on the job, the same grant ctx.writeAs already needs. The escape-hatch guard exempts jobs by name, so this surfaces only at runtime; grep your jobs for ctx.queryAs. Known consumer sites: offlot-app channel-text generate-texts.job, campaign-calendar sync, campaign-channel-foundation seed-starter-channels.

title: Entity events are versionable: eventVersion + eventMigrations on r.entity
detail: Entities can declare eventVersion and row-shaped eventMigrations; lifecycle events are stamped with the version and upcast on rebuild and aggregate load. A version bump invalidates entity snapshots.

title: excludeFields per verb reaches the renderer and the agent manifest
detail: WriteHandlerDef carries excludedFields; entityEdit screens get writeExcludedFields per verb. The edit form shows them read-only and keeps them out of the payload, create hides them, and the agent manifest lists them per handler.

title: Identity and tenant switches are explicitly gated; escape-hatch audit is durable
migration: Job ctx.writeAs now needs r.systemScope() on the feature or escapeHatch: { reason } on the job; use ctx.write when the job acts as its own system user. A payload tenantIdOverride is refused by the dispatcher for non-SystemAdmin callers (handlers no longer call crossTenantOverrideDenied, which is removed; use mayOverrideTenant for other cross-tenant fields). Entity convention handlers with a cross-tenant escapeHatch now keep the operator as actor in the row stream (executor option streamTenantId, system-mode db only). createEscapeHatchReporter requires log; pass the runtime logger and share one report window per runtime. EscapeHatchUseEvent and the audit sink payload gain an optional caller. Call flushEscapeHatchAudits() before closing the database on shutdown.

title: A failed nested ctx.write is rolled back to a savepoint instead of leaking its event and projection into the outer commit
detail: A nested `ctx.write` / `ctx.writeAs` (and workflow `call-feature`) now runs in a savepoint of the outer transaction: when the inner write fails after its event and projection were written, for example because an in-transaction hook throws, the inner change is rolled back even if the outer handler swallows the failure result and commits, and a SQL error in the inner write no longer poisons the outer transaction. The inner write's afterCommit hooks only run when it succeeded.

title: Unknown record ids show a localized empty state; an undecryptable encrypted field reads null instead of failing the whole list
detail: Edit and detail screens show a localized empty state with a way back to the list for an unknown or deleted record id instead of a hard-coded English banner, and an entity list or detail no longer fails with a 500 when one row's encrypted field cannot be decrypted: that field reads null, the rest of the row and list are served, and the failure is logged at error level with entity, row id and field

title: Executor list returns the stream version, so updates built on list rows no longer fail with version_conflict after ctx.appendEvent
Update schema accepts null on optional fields, so a preSave hook or client can clear a stored optional value
detail: Update schema accepts null on optional fields, so a preSave hook or client can clear a stored optional value without presave_hook_invalid_output or a validation error

title: detail() no longer pairs an old row with a newer stream version, so update({ version: detail.version }) cannot overwrite a concurrent write
detail:
`detail()` reads the row and the stream version in one statement and validates entity-cache hits against the stream version
Before, a concurrent update between the row read and the version read handed out the old row with the new version, so `update({ version: detail.version })` passed the optimistic lock and overwrote the newer write. A cached row whose version differs from the stream version now counts as a cache miss.

title: _refs respect access.read, the parentRef gate and field-level read of the referenced entity; unreadable refs are omitted and the renderer falls back to the UUID
detail:
`_refs` only carry what the caller may read on the referenced entity
Eagerload used to resolve every referenced row of the tenant, so a reference field pointing at a team- or row-scoped entity leaked rows the caller could not read themselves. It now applies the target entity's `access.read` (row/team scope), its parentRef gate and its field-level read access, still with one batched lookup per reference field. A reference the caller may not read is omitted exactly like a missing one (no existence oracle); the renderer falls back to the UUID. The handler-level `access` of the target's detail handler is not evaluated, the declarative `access.read` of the target entity is authoritative (same model as reference search and sort).
`enrichWithReferences` and `enrichRowWithReferences` take a required fifth argument `viewer: { user, parentVisibility }`. The old strip of PII/encrypted fields on ownership-scoped targets is gone: readable rows are decrypted, unreadable rows are not returned at all.

title: enrichWithReferences and enrichRowWithReferences require a viewer { user, parentVisibility }
migration: Custom handlers pass `{ user: query.user, parentVisibility: { entities: ctx.registry.getAllEntities() } }` as the fifth argument. No direct callers are known in the workspace apps. Apps can now point reference fields at team- or row-scoped entities (for example solon's unitId and propertyId).

title: crossTenant removed from entity convention handlers; write handlers with escapeHatch need SystemAdmin-only access
migration: Replace crossTenant: true with escapeHatch: { reason } (run bun node_modules/@cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/src/scripts/codemod/migrate-cross-tenant.ts, then replace its placeholder reason, which is rejected otherwise). A create/update/delete/restore handler with escapeHatch must declare access: { roles: ["SystemAdmin"] }; list and detail handlers keep their access.

title: ctx.queryAsMember read-only context now allowlists searchAdapter (search), redis (read commands) and entityCache (get, mget); other methods are denied
ctx.queryAsMember reads run under a statement timeout (DispatcherOptions.memberReadTimeoutMs, default 10000) and fail with member_read_timeout
ctx.queryProjection with unsafeAllTenants no longer demands a grant on projections without a tenant column
defineProjectionQueryHandler accepts unsafeAllTenants: { reason } as grant and audit reason
Event append without a transaction is atomic; ctx.outsideTransaction; pending-gap ranges merge and are exported as a gauge; seed scan starts at the highest consumer cursor
Failed job attempts are logged via the runner logger (job, jobId, attempt, final, error)
Field-level access.read with a where-rule now fails the boot (also on embedded sub-fields)
migration: Replace the where-rule on the field with a from()-rule (e.g. from("user:id", "ownerId")) or move the where-rule to entity access.read. Field read access is evaluated in memory and could never grant a where-rule, so it only hid the field.

title: kumiko_events gets a partial index over payload tenantId for tenant-membership streams
detail: The forget-cleanup membership-history queries filter on payload->>'tenantId' and scanned all of kumiko_events. createEventsTable now also ensures events_membership_payload_tenant_idx ON kumiko_events ((payload->>'tenantId')) WHERE aggregate_type = 'tenant-membership', built CONCURRENTLY with the same INVALID-rebuild and race handling as the idempotency index. No migration: the index is created on the next boot or schema apply. On a large event history the first build takes a while but does not block appends.

title: changes.json entries can set manualAfterCodemod to stay pending manual after the codemod ran
detail: A codemod entry with `manualAfterCodemod: true` is recorded in `pendingManual` of `.kumiko/upgrade-state.json` in addition to the codemod run. Set it with `kumiko changes add --codemod <path> --manual-after-codemod`.

title: read.findOne and read.findMany log a warning when a foreign where.tenantId is narrowed to the caller's tenant scope
requestContext.run and runAsDirectCallEntry removed from the public /api barrel; requestContext there is read-only
migration: Import run and runAsDirectCallEntry from @cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/internal/request-context; reserved for agent-tools and server runtime wiring, do not use to lift a handler past the risk floor. requestContext.get() from /api is unchanged.

title: SSE broadcasts, toggle sync, stream expiry, page-head abort, PII backfill failures and preSave output are now handled strictly instead of failing silently
detail: Review hardening: confirmed SSE publish awaited by consumers, feature-toggle cache invalidation over the cache-sync bus, stream expiry timer, page-head resolver abort signal, PII backfill `failed_event_ids`, preSave output validation, read-only proxy `then`/symbol guard, no orphan-row delete in event-consumer state, exported `DEFAULT_HTML` of dev-server and server-runtime

title: TenantDestroyHookResult: done:false now requires processed
migration: Tenant destroy hooks that return { done: false } must also return processed (number of items handled this tick). A tick with processed 0 now counts as a failed stage attempt.

title: Handler titles and field labels as i18n keys, plus the references Zod meta
detail: `handlerTitleKey(qn)` (`<qn>:title`) and `handlerFieldLabelKey(qn, field)` (`<qn>:field:<field>`) define where a handler's title and input labels live; a feature declares the full keys (e.g. `channel-texts:write:generate:title`, built with `handlerTitleKey(qn)`) in `r.translations`, because the client resolves keys without a feature prefix. Mark a handler input field that points at an entity with `vehicleId: z.string().meta({ references: "vehicle" })` (or `"feature:entity"`); boot throws when the entity is unknown and `handlerFieldReference(schema, field)` reads it. `findHandlerTranslationGaps` reports agent-exposed write handlers without an entity or actionForm screen and without these keys as `handler-without-translation`. `kumiko agent lint` lists them as warnings without affecting the exit code, and the boot prints one summary line. `findAgentDocGaps` stays unchanged on purpose, since the agent-manifest guard fails on every gap it returns.

title: list search no longer drops hits beyond the 50th candidate
detail: event-store-executor list: the search path now asks the SearchAdapter for up to 1000 candidate ids instead of the adapter's default 50, so hits beyond the 50th are no longer silently dropped. When the adapter returns the full 1000 (Meilisearch's maxTotalHits cap), the list result carries `searchTruncated: true` (new optional field on `CursorResult`) so clients can tell the match set may be incomplete.

title: The blockDelete-without-anonymize boot warning names the retention-cron risk instead of a Forget error
detail: The boot warning for `retention.strategy: "blockDelete"` without a field `anonymize` now names the real risk: once keepFor expires, the data-retention cron anonymizes nothing and the row keeps its PII

title: db.global(table) writes on executor-managed entity tables are rejected
detail:
Database, event-store consumer, search and Redis review fixes
`db.global(table)` writes are rejected on executor-managed entity tables, and `unsafeRaw` handles derived through `begin`, `transaction` or `reserve` keep the personal-data gate. Reference sorting and search re-check label and read access plus ownership, and a stale search index can no longer surface another tenant's row. A cross-tenant convention handler reports one audit event per touched row with that row as target.
A failing dispatcher pass no longer records its error on a consumer whose cursor moved in the meantime and skips a row another pass holds locked. A projection rebuild aborts when the configured blind-index key differs from the one used to build the live table. An array `ne` filter on a jsonb column means "does not contain all of these", matching the entity list filter. `date` columns that still hold a timestamptz log a warning once per column.
`kumiko_event_dispatcher_listen_connected` only drops to 0 on a real connection-loss error and is restored when the pre-check recovers. A consumer logs once when it tracks more than 1000 pending gap ranges. The lazy Meilisearch default config no longer overwrites settings stored by an earlier `configure()` after a restart.
Access invalidation publishes through `PubSubSignal.publishConfirmed`, so a Redis failure fails the consumer and the event is redelivered instead of being dropped (`SseBroker.publishAccessInvalidation` may return a promise). `KUMIKO_REDIS_CHANNEL_PREFIX` namespaces the SSE and feature-toggle Pub/Sub channels for apps sharing one Redis; `createRedisToggleSyncSignal` takes the prefix as an optional third argument. Types that mention `Temporal` now carry the `temporal-polyfill/global` reference into their `.d.ts` files.
migration: Write entities through the entity executor and keep db.global for hand-written unmanaged tables.

title: unsafeRaw handles derived through begin, transaction or reserve keep the personal-data gate
A stale search index can no longer surface another tenant's row
A projection rebuild aborts when the blind-index key differs from the one used to build the live table
An array ne filter on a jsonb column means "does not contain all of these"
Access invalidation publishes with confirmation so a Redis failure redelivers the event
defineFeature throws when dedupeOptions holds a nested object
migration: Flatten dedupeOptions to primitive values.

title: Boot validation rejects an object-form redirect with idFrom on a screen that has no id
migration: Point the redirect at a screen with an id or drop idFrom.

title: A list column absent from the query output schema must set virtual: true
migration: Add virtual: true to computed columns that are not part of the query output.

title: Session-only httpRoutes now pass the global IP rate limit
Boot validator rejects inert sortable, authored urlPrefillFields and an unknown listScreenId
migration: Remove sortable from entityList columns and sortable true from projectionList columns (declare sorting on the entity field), remove urlPrefillFields from form screens (buildAppSchema derives it from navigate params), and point listScreenId at a mounted screen short id.

title: TreeAction is screen XOR target at the type level
migration: Give every createAction and actions[] entry either screen or target, not both and not neither; the boot validator already rejected the other forms.

title: Row actions can open a secretMint or actionForm that submits without edits
detail: actionForm and secretMint screens gain `submitPrefilled`: a row action that navigates in with `params` can submit the form right away, with the record id carried in a hidden or read-only field.

title: Select field options can depend on another field
detail: Select fields gain `conditionalOptions`: options that are only available while a condition on a sibling field holds, filtered in the form and enforced on write.

title: setupTestStack accepts rateLimitNowMs to freeze the rate-limit clock in tests
detail: setupTestStack accepts `rateLimitNowMs`, the time source of the stack's rate-limit resolver, so tests can freeze the token-bucket clock instead of racing the refill window

title: Boot validation rejects public-intake handlers without rate limit and serial-id unmanaged entities with recordOwned fields
detail:
Boot validation rejects `personalData: "public-intake"` handlers with `rateLimit: { disabled: true }` and unmanaged `idType: "serial"` entities with `recordOwned` fields
Both combinations were silently accepted before: the first left an anonymous personal-data write without its only abuse protection, the second produced record-owned ciphertext that `forgetSubject` can never shred.

title: r.crud accepts per-verb agent hints and dedupeFeatures no longer drops a same-named feature that registers different handlers
detail:
`r.crud` takes per-verb `agents` hints, and same-named features only dedupe when their registered surface matches
`registerEntityCrud` accepts `agents: { delete: { risk: "high" } }` so one irreversible verb can be raised without raising create/update. `dedupeFeatures` additionally requires equal entity and handler key sets before collapsing two same-named features with equal `dedupeOptions`; otherwise it throws the existing duplicate-feature error instead of silently dropping the second one. `i18nKey()` marks live on a `globalThis` registry so two installed framework copies agree.

title: Event piiFields reject owner field "id" instead of encrypting under a phantom user key
detail:
`defineEvent` rejects `personal: { of: "id" }` in `piiFields` at boot
On entities `of: "id"` means record-owned, but on events it encrypted under a user key named after the payload id, which a forget never reaches, so crypto-shredding silently did nothing. Declare a record-owned event field with `personal: "self"` instead.

title: Webhook signature 401 hides verify() error details; boot rejects silently dropped drawer prefills, colliding secret field ids and unlintable where-rule tables
detail:
Signature extra routes no longer return the verify() error text in the 401 body, drawer prefill and secret field ids fail at boot when they would silently misbehave
A non-`ExtraRouteRejection` throw from a signature route's `verify()` now answers with the generic message "signature verification failed" and logs the detail server-side. Boot now rejects a drawer `params` prefill that targets a sensitive or password field or a field the target layout does not render, a secrets screen whose field ids collide across hyphenated feature names, and a where-rule subquery on a table whose column set cannot be derived.

title: Unknown status tones fail boot and secretMint confirm actions respect role gating
detail:
Stricter boot checks and role projection for screens and handlers
Inline handler registration without `options.access` now throws immediately, a section with `fields: []` and `groups: []` fails boot, and unknown tones in `header.statusTones` or select `optionTones` fail boot instead of dropping the badge colour. The renderer falls back to the value heuristic for an unknown tone, and `statusToneForOptionTone` now returns `undefined` for it. `secretMint` confirm-step actions are stripped for roles that cannot see the target screen.
Entity convention `create` handlers keep tenant-filtered lookups even when the handler declares `escapeHatch`/`crossTenant`. Duplicate `waitForEvent` steps on the same `awaits` event are rejected when the workflow pipeline is built. An empty `PROMETHEUS_METRICS_TOKEN` counts as unset instead of failing boot.
`GET /api/sse` now closes itself when the JWT it was opened with expires. File uploads must attach to a registered file field (a non-file field answers 400 `unresolvable_field`), and a `.docx` upload must be a ZIP containing `word/` entries. Signature extra routes outside `/api` get the request-body cap (`maxRequestBytes`) before their body is read. `EXT_USER_DATA` registrations with neither an export nor a delete hook fail boot. The dashboard updated-at stamp follows live refetches and retries.
Text fields accept `minLength` (enforced by the generated write schema), `enumOption` renders array values per entry, list columns can opt out of sorting with `sortable: false`, and `BUILT_IN_MEMBERSHIP_ROLES` exposes the ranked membership roles. The PAT list translates its scopes column, MFA code fields enforce their minimum length, plan checkout no longer repeats the billing-enabled and active-subscription gates.

title: appendEventInTenantDb and getStreamVersionInTenantDb append and read stream versions through a TenantDb, optionally running inline projections
detail:
`appendEventInTenantDb` appends an event on a TenantDb's own connection or transaction
Framework-side code that holds a `TenantDb` (for example inside `runInOwnTransaction`) could not append to the event store without a raw runner. `appendEventInTenantDb(tenantDb, event, { registry })` and `getStreamVersionInTenantDb(tenantDb, aggregateId)` from `@cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/event-store` do it: the tenant is always the TenantDb's own, the append goes through `append()` (PII encryption, origin stamping), and with `registry` the inline projections run on the same runner.

title: Rate-limited, denied or invalid callers no longer consume cap usage or trigger soft-warn, because pre-handler gates run before reserveBeforeTransaction
reserveBeforeTransaction may return a ReservationHandle whose confirmInTransaction settles the reservation inside the handler transaction
Seeds can find template rows with ctx.findTemplateResources
detail: Seeds can replace a raw SELECT … FROM read_template_resources with ctx.findTemplateResources, which binds every filter value as a parameter.

title: Boot validation and the client schema cover select optionsAvailabilityQuery on entity and screen fields
kumiko-upgrade advances in one --apply run, tracks open manual migrations with ids and resolves them via --resolve
detail:
kumiko-upgrade: one --apply run advances, manual items are resolved with --resolve
`--apply` now moves the marker to the installed version in a single run. Breaking changes without a codemod stay in the marker as `pendingManual` with a stable id (`<version>:<8-char title hash>`) and are listed after every run; the upgrade guard no longer fails on them. `--resolve <id|version>[,...] --reason "<text>" [--not-applicable]` moves entries to `resolvedManual` (version must match exactly one open entry; unknown refs write nothing). Resolved ids do not come back. The plain report lists open entries, and `--json` carries them as `pendingManual`.
migration: If you relied on a second --apply to acknowledge manual migrations, run kumiko-upgrade --resolve <id> --reason "<text>" instead.

title: runSeedWritesAt runs regular writes with a caller-set event time, only in seed mode
detail:
runSeedWritesAt: regular writes with a caller-set event time for E2E and demo seeds
`runSeedWritesAt(createdAt, fn)` from `@cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/event-store` runs `fn` so that every event appended inside it is stored with `createdAt` instead of the database `now()`. The writes still go through the normal path (handler, validation, event append, projections), so projections that read the event time, such as entity `insertedAt`/`modifiedAt`, see the back-dated value. The helper only works with `KUMIKO_TEST_SEED=1` and `NODE_ENV` other than `production`; otherwise it throws `SeedModeDisabledError` before `fn` runs. `buildServer` now refuses to boot when `KUMIKO_TEST_SEED=1` is set together with `NODE_ENV=production`. Nothing from a request (payload, headers, seed-route body) can set the time; call the helper from an in-process seeder such as an `extraSeeders` entry or a `runDevApp` seed function. Events keep their global id order, so back-dated events are still delivered to consumers; only `created_at` order differs. A seed write dated before its stream predecessor is rejected, because `loadAggregateAsOf` and projection rebuilds order by `created_at`. Events written by async consumers or jobs in reaction to a seeded event are not back-dated; the seeder has to write those itself inside the scope. Await everything inside `fn`.
migration: Seeders that need history (for example 90 days of status changes) wrap their dispatcher or ctx.write calls in `runSeedWritesAt(createdAt, async () => { ... })` instead of writing events or projection rows directly. Boot the server with `KUMIKO_TEST_SEED=1` and a non-production `NODE_ENV`; a boot with both the flag and `NODE_ENV=production` now fails. Within one aggregate stream, write the events in ascending time.

title: Dispatch routes reject malformed or type-less request bodies with 400 instead of 500
detail:
Dispatch routes answer 400 for unusable request bodies
`/api/write`, `/api/query`, `/api/command`, `/api/batch` and `/api/stream` return a validation error (400) for malformed JSON, a non-object body or a missing handler `type`. Before, those requests ended in an unclassified 500. `/api/auth/switch-tenant` treats a non-object body like a missing `tenantId`.

title: Missing-instance-id warning and docs reflect shared SSE delivery and recommend the pod name
detail:
Boot warning and docs no longer claim SSE is per instance
The built-in SSE consumers share one cursor since fw#2625 and fw#2630. The missing-`KUMIKO_INSTANCE_ID` warning, the consumer-state comment and `docs/reference/infra-requirements.md` now say what the id is still for (the `app.started` event and per-instance consumers) and recommend the pod name.

title: A request costs one rate-limit token per bucket even when the handler nests queryAs or ctx.query calls into handlers sharing that bucket
detail:
Nested dispatches no longer charge a rate-limit bucket twice
A handler that calls `ctx.query`, `ctx.queryAs` or `ctx.write` into another handler with a limit on the same bucket (for example `per: "ip"`) used to cost two tokens per request. Each entry dispatch now charges a bucket once, and nested calls reuse that charge. Nested handlers that limit a different bucket are still limited, and every command of a batch still charges on its own. The public `/media` route had half its advertised limit because of this.

title: TenantDbs built from unsafeRaw() and file routes run custom projections
detail:
A TenantDb rebuilt from `unsafeRaw()` runs custom projections again
`ctx.db.unsafeRaw()` used to return the bare connection unless a public-intake gate was active. A `createTenantDb(ctx.db.unsafeRaw(), …)` inside a handler, hook or job therefore lost the projection registry, and its writes skipped custom projections. `unsafeRaw()` now returns a runner bound to the registry (and the gate, if any) whenever one is present. The file routes pass the app registry to their TenantDbs, so file events reach custom projections as well.
migration: `unsafeRaw()` on a dispatcher or job TenantDb now returns a proxy instead of the raw connection object. Code that compares the runner by identity with the raw connection must compare against the proxy instead. Standalone seeds that call createTenantDb on a raw connection still have no registry; seed through dispatcher.write. Code that re-ran custom projections by hand after such a write (on a reloaded event, not the returned one) must drop that call, or the projection applies twice. File upload and delete now run custom projections on fileRef events inside the same transaction, so a failing projection rolls the upload back like for any other entity.

title: App error reasons only carry a docsUrl when errorDocs covers them
detail:
`docsUrl` in error responses is now resolved at serialization by `resolveErrorDocsUrl`. Framework reasons (and errors without a reason) link to the framework docs as before. An app's own reasons no longer link to the framework docs, where no page exists for them: they get a `docsUrl` only if the new option `errorDocs: { baseUrl, reasons: string[] | "all" }` (on `runProdApp`, `buildServer`, `createKumikoServer`, `setupTestStack`) covers them.
Migration: `KumikoError.docsUrl` (the getter) is removed; use `resolveErrorDocsUrl(err, errorDocs?)`. `ErrorResponseBody.docsUrl` is now optional. Apps whose clients read `docsUrl` for app reasons pass `errorDocs` or handle the missing field.
migration: KumikoError.docsUrl (the getter) is removed; call resolveErrorDocsUrl(err, errorDocs?) instead. ErrorResponseBody.docsUrl is optional. Apps whose clients read docsUrl for app reasons pass errorDocs or handle the missing field.

title: Executor writes outside the dispatcher no longer skip custom projections
detail:
Executor writes run custom projections
`EventStoreExecutor` create, update, delete, forget and restore now run the custom projections registered for the written event, in the same savepoint as the write. The registry is bound to the `TenantDb` by the dispatcher and the job runner; a `TenantDb` built elsewhere skips custom projections. Projection runs are idempotent per event object, so the dispatcher's own pass after the handler does not run them twice.
migration: Remove manual `runProjections` calls after executor writes in hooks or jobs together with the bump. A call is a no-op only when it passes the exact event object the executor returned; a spread or rebuilt event projects twice.

title: isFailedWriteResult is exported from the pipeline entry
detail:
`isFailedWriteResult` and `FailedWriteResult` are exported from the pipeline entry
Consumers can narrow a `WriteResult` to its failure branch with `import { isFailedWriteResult } from "@cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/pipeline"` instead of re-implementing the check.

title: retiredCookieDomains clears auth cookies left on a former cookieDomain
detail: `AuthRoutesConfig.retiredCookieDomains` lists domains that used to carry the auth cookies. Login and logout also send delete headers for `kumiko_auth` and `kumiko_csrf` with `Domain=<entry>`, so a stale cookie from an earlier `cookieDomain` no longer shadows the new session after the value changes. Login sends these deletes before the new `Set-Cookie` headers. `createAuthRoutes` throws on an empty entry, on `;`, comma, whitespace, CR or LF, and on an entry equal to the current `cookieDomain`. Without the option nothing changes. Remove an entry once the session TTL has passed since the switch.

title: Test stacks validate nav references and can run the full boot validation
detail: `setupTestStack` now validates nav, workspace and tree-action references on the mounted features, with the same error messages as the prod boot.
